Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Chat.Android/index..title: Uniform.Chat.Android | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Chat.Android/index..summary: Uniform.Chat.Android The Android entry point of the graphical app in Uniform.Chat.Avalonia: the activity, the manifest and the resources. MainApplication sets XDG_DATA_HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME to the app's private files folder before anything else runs, so AppDirectories and the engine need no Android code. The activity resizes for the keyboard. Android backup is off, so encryption keys stay on the device. Build and install The Android app is in Uniform.Chat.slnx, so building the whole solution needs the Android workload; it also needs the Android SDK and JDK 17: dotnet workload install android dotnet build src/Uniform.Chat.Android -t:Install \ -p:AndroidSdkDirectory=$HOME/Android/Sdk -p:JavaSdkDirectory=/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk-amd64 -t:Install installs the debug build on the phone connected with USB debugging (adb devices lists it). To reach a server running on the computer, forward its port and sign in with http://localhost:8008: adb reverse tcp:8008 tcp:8008 Background work Two foreground services keep the app working off screen, each with a notification: SyncForegroundService keeps syncing while the app is in the background or the screen is off; without it, Android's restricted networking cuts the app off. Its type is specialUse, as no other type fits a connection to the user's own server, with the reason in the android.app.PROPERTY_SPECIAL_USE_FGS_SUBTYPE property; Google Play reviews that reason. CallForegroundService keeps a call going: of the types phoneCall and microphone, which needs the MANAGE_OWN_CALLS permission. Google Play asks for each type to be declared under App content → Foreground service permissions, with a short video of the user starting it, and for USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT, which rings incoming calls over the lock screen. Call audio The microphone and speaker of a call share Android's communication mode for the length of the call (CommunicationMode): in it, the phone routes voice to the earpiece and runs its echo cancellation between the speaker and the microphone. The microphone records from the voice communication source and also turns on the platform's echo canceller and noise suppressor, kept for the whole recording, since a collected effect is released. Policies The sign-in form links to the user policy and privacy policy in the user guide, at their GitHub addresses; Google Play needs the privacy policy's address too.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Chat.Avalonia/index.title: Uniform.Chat.Avalonia | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Chat.Avalonia/index.summary: Uniform.Chat.Avalonia The graphical app, in Avalonia 12 with the Fluent theme and CommunityToolkit.Mvvm. The same views run in a desktop window and as the single view of the Android activity; GuiPlatform carries what differs: the application name (and so the data folders), the device name shown to other sessions, whether the screen is always one pane, and extra services. Hosts AccountPaths needs Matrix:UserId when the services are built, so the app has no host until someone signs in. ClientConnection.StartAsync builds a HostApplicationBuilder per sign-in: AddSettings, the user ID and server from the form as in-memory configuration, AddMatrixClient, and GuiCredentialPrompt, which returns the form's password or throws PasswordRequiredException when a resumed session needs one. Signing out or in again disposes the host and builds a new one. AccountMemory keeps the last user ID in the settings file, so the next start resumes without the form. SettingsViewModel keeps the theme, text size and notification switch in its Ui section and saves on every change; App applies the theme as RequestedThemeVariant and the text size as Fluent's ControlContentThemeFontSize. Not yet covered Renaming devices, and notifications on Windows and Android.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Chat.Avalonia/view-.title: View models | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Chat.Avalonia/view-.summary: View models MainViewModel switches Page between LoginViewModel, ConnectingViewModel and ChatViewModel; MainView picks the view by data template. ChatViewModel follows the engine's events on a background task: it reads SyncProcessor.Changes and posts each batch to the UI thread through IUiDispatcher, where room state is read under SyncProcessor.Read. ConnectionStatus.Changed, EventsDecrypted and OutboxSender.RoomChanged are posted the same way. Each posted change runs inside a try/catch that logs, as an exception on the UI thread would end the app. MessageList turns events into MessageViewModel items. Edits, deletions and reactions change the item they refer to instead of adding one, also when older history arrives after them. Unsent outbox messages are shown last; their list is reloaded on every outbox change, and a version counter drops loads that finish out of order, so a sent message never comes back as pending. Room creation, invites, deletions, typing notices, read markers and file uploads call MatrixClient directly; messages, replies, edits and reactions go through the outbox. Files to encrypted rooms are encrypted with UploadEncryptedAsync and their message is sent through the outbox, which encrypts it. SecurityViewModel shows GetSecurityStatusAsync and offers set-up, recovery or verification by what is missing; it waits for CryptoService.WhenStarted, as encryption starts after sign-in. Setting up recovery asks for the password only when the server answers with a user-interactive auth challenge. ChatViewModel follows CryptoService.VerificationChanged and shows one VerificationViewModel at a time, so incoming requests and our own requests go through the same panel. ChatViewModel also decides on notifications: new messages in direct chats, messages whose m.mentions name the user or the room, and invites that were not in the list before, at most three per sync and none from history or the first sync. They are passed to GuiPlatform.Notifier unless the window has the focus on that room. The desktop app sets FreeDesktopNotifier on Linux, which calls org.freedesktop.Notifications.Notify over the session bus with Tmds.DBus.Protocol, the D-Bus library Avalonia already uses.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Chat.Avalonia/views.title: Views | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Chat.Avalonia/views.summary: Views ChatView has the room list and the open room side by side, or one at a time below 720 pixels and always on phones. It keeps the newest message in view while scrolled to the bottom, loads older messages at the top, and goes back to the list on TopLevel.BackRequested (Android's back button). RichText is a SelectableTextBlock that parses a message's formatted_body with AngleSharp into inlines: emphasis, code, headings, quotes, lists, links and mention pills; reply fallbacks are dropped. Without HTML it shows the plain body. File dialogs use TopLevel.StorageProvider, which is the system picker on both platforms. The message box's keys are handled in the tunnel phase: a multi-line TextBox takes Enter and Ctrl+V itself, so a bubbling handler never sees them. Pasting checks the clipboard for files, then an image, and falls back to the box's own text paste. Links: RichText records the character range of each link while building its inlines (a LineBreak counts as one character) and hit-tests TextLayout on click, as Avalonia has no inline hyperlink. Plain-text bodies get their web addresses linked. Bindings are compiled (x:DataType), so binding errors fail the build.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Chat.Desktop/index..title: Uniform.Chat.Desktop | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Chat.Desktop/index..summary: Uniform.Chat.Desktop The Windows and Linux entry point of the graphical app in Uniform.Chat.Avalonia: it starts Avalonia with a desktop window, and on Linux sets FreeDesktopNotifier as the app's notifier and ships install-desktop-entry.sh, which adds the app to the application menu. Build and run The desktop app builds with the rest of the solution: dotnet run --project src/Uniform.Chat.Desktop The program file is Uniform.Chat (Uniform.Chat.exe on Windows), not the project's name: file managers on Linux match names ending in .Desktop to .desktop launchers regardless of case, and would not run it. Releases publish it as a self-contained single file for linux-x64, linux-arm64, win-x64 and win-arm64; see Building.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Chat.Server/index.h.title: Uniform.Chat.Server | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Chat.Server/index.h.summary: Uniform.Chat.Server The server application: it reads settings with AddSettings, writes one log file per session, adds the engine of Uniform.Matrix.Server, and runs with the Terminal.Gui dashboard or without it (Host:Ui, see ServerHostOptions). The dashboard has the settings, users, rooms and logs windows; user management goes through AdminService, which logs each change at Information level. The program file is uniform-chat-server (uniform-chat-server.exe on Windows), as the system service is named. Program sets the application name uniform-chat-server, the same as the assembly's, as ASP.NET loads the assembly of that name at start; it names the settings and data folders, e.g. ~/.config/uniform-chat-server and ~/.local/share/uniform-chat-server. Before the name Uniform Chat they were uniform-matrix-server-host; the server does not move them, the user guide's Updating article does. Start-up errors that people can fix themselves are shown in two lines instead of a stack trace: a listen address that is already in use, with a hint about --Urls, and a TLS certificate that cannot be read, naming the setting and path. The full exception stays in the log file. With Turn:Enabled, EmbeddedTurn adds the STUN and TURN server of Uniform.Stun.Hosting and connects it to the homeserver's calls. With LiveKit:Enabled, EmbeddedLiveKit serves the MatrixRTC authorization service of Uniform.LiveKit.Hosting at /livekit/jwt. It checks the homeserver's own OpenID tokens in its store, without a round trip, and those of other servers over federation. Its IRoomMembership gives tokens only to users joined to the call's room, by the room's current state on this homeserver, which also holds remote users of the rooms it is in. Unless they are set, LiveKit:FullAccessHomeservers becomes the server name, and Calls:LiveKitServiceUrl becomes the service at Server:PublicBaseUrl. How to run it, as a service too, is in the server's user guide.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Chat.Terminal/index.title: Uniform.Chat.Terminal | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Chat.Terminal/index.summary: Uniform.Chat.Terminal The terminal app: Program calls AddSettings, AddMatrixClient and registers its UiOptions, then runs the UI. The program file is Uniform.Chat (Uniform.Chat.exe on Windows), like the desktop app's. Program sets the host's application name to Uniform.Chat.Terminal, because the settings, data and log folders are named after it, not after the program file. User interface Program creates the Terminal.Gui application first, starts the host's background services and then runs MainWindow on the main thread until the user quits. Background work never touches views directly: sync changes, outbox changes and connection status are marshalled with IApplication.Invoke, and the password prompt shows its dialog the same way. MainWindow lays out the menu bar, room list, TimelinePane, member list, input line and status bar, and handles menu actions, /commands and keys. Shortcuts are handled application-wide in one key handler; menu items only show them. TimelinePane is a ListView of wrapped lines. It rewraps on resize, colors lines by EntryKind, inserts day separators, keeps pending outbox messages last and follows new lines while scrolled to the bottom. MainWindow.Messages.cs holds message actions (reply, react, edit, delete, save), compose modes, typing notifications, nick completion, file sending and the devices dialog. Replies, edits and reactions go through the outbox like messages; uploads and redactions are sent directly. MainWindow.Images.cs shows image previews. An entry with an ImageUri asks TimelinePane.PreviewProvider for lines on every rebuild; the first request starts a background load of an 800×600 thumbnail through MediaCache (falling back to the full image), decodes it with StbImageSharp into DecodedImage, then refreshes the pane. AsciiArt.Render samples a brightness grid (one value per cell, or 2×4 per cell for Braille), stretches its contrast, then maps it to shade blocks ░▒▓█ with Floyd–Steinberg dithering between the five levels, to the 70-step ASCII ramp, or to dithered Braille dots. It corrects for cells being about twice as tall as wide. Previews fill the pane unless limited in settings and are cached per image and size; the pane rebuilds on height changes while it shows images. The viewer feeds a downscaled image to Terminal.Gui's ImageView, which uses Kitty or Sixel graphics when available. MessageFormatter and TextWrapper are pure functions and unit-tested. Wrapping counts terminal columns, so emoji and CJK take two. A dialog opened from another dialog's result is queued with IApplication.Invoke; opening it directly lets the key that closed the first dialog reach the second. Terminal.Gui 2.5 does not report F3 when the terminal sends ESC O R (most xterm-style terminals do), so message selection is on Ctrl+Up. Reading Room state for display goes through SyncProcessor.Read, as RoomStore is not thread-safe. History and member loading fetch from the server outside the lock and apply inside it.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.LiveKit.Authorizati.title: Uniform.LiveKit.Authorization | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.LiveKit.Authorizati.summary: Uniform.LiveKit.Authorization A MatrixRTC authorization service that behaves like lk-jwt-service. Element Call, Element X and other MatrixRTC clients ask it for LiveKit tokens. LiveKitAuthorizer handles both requests: It checks the fields. A missing one answers 400 M_BAD_JSON. It asks the token's homeserver who the token belongs to, through an IOpenIdVerifier. The user must belong to that same homeserver, as a homeserver could otherwise vouch for anyone. In /get_token, the user must also be the member's claimed user. When the authorizer was given an IRoomMembership, the user must also be joined to the Matrix room. A service inside a homeserver knows that from the room's state; lk-jwt-service and a standalone service don't check it. Every failure answers 401 M_UNAUTHORIZED with the same text. Users of FullAccessHomeservers get the room created in LiveKit first. The room waits 5 minutes for its first participant and stays 20 seconds after the last one leaves. Their token may publish. Other users only subscribe, and only to rooms that exist. They may not hand over a delayed leave event (delay_id). It answers with LiveKit's URL and a token that holds for an hour. FederationOpenIdVerifier asks /_matrix/federation/v1/openid/userinfo. It goes to the server name's m.server delegation, or to the name itself, at port 8448 when no port is given. Delayed leaves A full-access member may hand its delayed leave event (MSC4140) to the service, with delay_id and delay_timeout in its token request, or at /delegate_delayed_leave. Element Call looks for that endpoint first, and hands its leave over when the endpoint answers anything but 404. Its device then restarts the leave only every 5 minutes instead of every 4 seconds. DelayedLeaveKeeper keeps each handed-over leave: It waits for the member to appear in its LiveKit room, asking LiveKit's room service. While the member stays, it restarts the delayed event at four fifths of its delay, at most an hour, as lk-jwt-service does. When LiveKit no longer has the member, checked every 5 seconds, it sends the leave at once, so the call membership ends. It acts on the delayed events through IDelayedEvents. HomeserverDelayedEvents finds the member's homeserver by its server name's /.well-known/matrix/client, never by the delay_cs_api_url the client gives, so the service only calls homeservers. The service inside Uniform Chat Server acts on its own users' delayed events directly. LiveKit needs no webhooks for this. The jobs live in memory: after a restart of the service, a member's homeserver sends the leave when its delay runs out. Uniform Chat Server keeps its delayed events in its database, so they also outlast a restart of the homeserver.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.LiveKit.Hosting/ind.title: Uniform.LiveKit.Hosting | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.LiveKit.Hosting/ind.summary: Uniform.LiveKit.Hosting AddLiveKitAuthorization binds LiveKitOptions to section LiveKit, and lists it among the settings with AddOptionSection. It registers a LiveKitAuthorizer that reads the current settings at each request, so changes need no restart. The API secret is marked secret. It also registers a FederationOpenIdVerifier, unless the host registered another IOpenIdVerifier first. Requests go through the named HTTP client HttpClientName, which tests can point at fakes. MapLiveKitAuthorization serves the endpoints of lk-jwt-service under a prefix: Endpoint Answer POST /get_token, POST /sfu/get {url, jwt}, or a Matrix error with its status OPTIONS of those 200 with CORS headers, for Element Call in a browser Other methods of those 405 GET /healthz, HEAD /healthz 200 While LiveKit:Enabled is false, the endpoints answer 404 M_UNRECOGNIZED. Uniform.Chat.Server embeds it at /livekit/jwt, and Uniform.LiveKit.Server runs it alone.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.LiveKit.Protocol/in.title: Uniform.LiveKit.Protocol | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.LiveKit.Protocol/in.summary: Uniform.LiveKit.Protocol What MatrixRTC calls and their authorization service exchange, with no network code. LiveKit's signalling messages, such as SignalRequest, SignalResponse and JoinResponse in the namespace LiveKit.Proto, are generated with Google.Protobuf from LiveKit's own protocol files in Protos/, copied unchanged. AccessToken holds the claims of a LiveKit access token. Sign makes the HS256 JWT with an API secret, and TryRead checks one. VideoGrant is its video claim, the room permissions. Unset permissions are left out, as LiveKit reads some missing ones as allowed. MatrixRtcNames makes LiveKit room names and participant identities as lk-jwt-service does. Each is the SHA-256 of a JSON array of strings, in unpadded Base64. The array is escaped as Rust's serde_json escapes it, so every client and service arrives at the same name. The legacy /sfu/get identity is @user:server:DEVICE in plain text. The JSON bodies of the service: TokenRequest of /get_token, LegacySfuRequest of /sfu/get, and SfuResponse answering both. Failures answer with AuthorizationError.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.LiveKit.Server/inde.title: Uniform.LiveKit.Server | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.LiveKit.Server/inde.summary: Uniform.LiveKit.Server The standalone MatrixRTC authorization service, uniform-livekit-server, a drop-in replacement for lk-jwt-service in front of a LiveKit server. It is an ASP.NET host with AddSettings, one log file per session and the console, and AddLiveKitAuthorization. It serves the endpoints at the root, at port 8080, as lk-jwt-service does. It also reads lk-jwt-service's environment variables (LIVEKIT_URL, LIVEKIT_KEY, LIVEKIT_SECRET, their _FILE forms, LIVEKIT_FULL_ACCESS_HOMESERVERS and LIVEKIT_JWT_BIND), so an existing container setup keeps working. They rank above the settings file and below the program's own environment variables and command line. Without LiveKit's URL, key, secret or full-access homeservers, it prints what is missing and exits with 1. Its settings and data folders are ~/.config/uniform-livekit-server and ~/.local/share/uniform-livekit-server. The LiveKit server itself is not part of it. How to run it is in its user guide.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.LiveKit/index.html.title: Uniform.LiveKit | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.LiveKit/index.html.summary: Uniform.LiveKit A LiveKit client in C#, for MatrixRTC calls, and clients of LiveKit's HTTP services. Joining a room LiveKitSignalClient is LiveKit's signalling: a WebSocket to the server's /rtc with protobuf messages each way, and pings at the interval the server asks. It joins with two peer connections, the way LiveKit's clients did before the single one. LiveKitRoom is a participant in a room. The server offers the subscriber connection, with a section for each track of the others, and offers it again as tracks come and go. PublishAsync announces the microphone and the camera with AddTrackRequest, then offers them on a send-only publisher connection. IdentityOf tells whose a received stream is, from the msid of its section. Both connections are AudioPeerConnections of Uniform.Matrix.WebRtc. FrameCryptor encrypts frames end to end as LiveKit's clients and Element Call do. Each frame keeps its first bytes in the clear (1 of Opus, 10 of a VP8 keyframe, 3 of other VP8 frames) and carries AES-GCM ciphertext, its IV and the key's index. Keys come from raw keys through HKDF-SHA-256 with the salt LKFrameEncryptionKey. LiveKitMedia makes a call's rooms one IMediaConnection: it encrypts this side's frames on the room it publishes to, and decrypts the others' with each sender's key on the rooms it subscribes to. HTTP services Over an HttpClient the caller gives: MatrixRtcAuthorizationClient sends a Matrix OpenID token to the authorization service named by a homeserver's rtc_foci. It gets back LiveKit's URL and an access token for the call. LiveKitRoomService calls LiveKit's room service over Twirp with JSON. Each call carries a one-minute token signed with the API secret. CreateRoomAsync creates a call's room, and keeps a room that already exists. The messages are in Uniform.LiveKit.Protocol. Tests Uniform.LiveKit.Tests checks the frame encryption against frames made with Python's cryptography in LiveKit's layout. With LIVEKIT_SERVER naming LiveKit's server program, it also starts one on loopback. One participant publishes encrypted audio and VP8 video, and another must receive and decrypt them.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Audio/index..title: Uniform.Matrix.Audio | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Audio/index..summary: Uniform.Matrix.Audio Voice audio for calls, the first part of calling: microphone and speaker through NAudio, and the Opus codec through Concentus, a pure C# port of libopus. Nothing here knows about Matrix or the network; Uniform.Matrix.Calls builds calls on it. Voice frames Calls carry voice as 20 ms frames of 48 kHz mono 16-bit samples (VoiceFormat), each one an Opus packet: VoiceEncoder encodes a frame, tuned for speech: the VoIP application, 32 kbit/s by default, and in-band forward error correction. VoiceDecoder decodes a packet back into a frame; given no packet, it conceals the loss from the frames before. Concentus would switch to a native libopus where it finds one; both classes turn that off, so every platform runs the same code. Devices IAudioDevices opens a platform's microphone as an NAudio IWaveIn and its speaker as an IWavePlayer. AudioDevices.ForThisPlatform returns: Platform Class Through Linux AlsaAudioDevices NAudio.Alsa's AlsaIn and AlsaOut on ALSA's default devices, which desktops route through PipeWire or PulseAudio Windows WasapiAudioDevices NAudio.Wasapi, in shared mode Android AndroidAudioDevices in Uniform.Chat.Android Android's AudioRecord from the voice communication source, with the phone's echo cancellation and noise suppression, and AudioTrack as call audio on the earpiece or the loudspeaker Devices record and play in their own formats. MicrophoneFrames turns any IWaveIn into voice frames, mixing channels to mono and resampling to 48 kHz; SpeakerFrames plays frames through any IWavePlayer, with a short buffer against uneven arrival and silence in the gaps. ALSA's default devices convert formats themselves; WASAPI's shared mode doesn't change sample rates, so on Windows the speaker resamples voice to the device's mix format, such as 44.1 kHz stereo, before handing it over. Hearing yourself VoiceLoopback plays the microphone back through the speaker, through Opus and a delay, to test the whole path without a call. The terminal client's /audiotest runs it: IAudioDevices devices = AudioDevices.ForThisPlatform() ?? throw new PlatformNotSupportedException(); using VoiceLoopback loopback = new(devices, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1)); loopback.Start(); Choosing devices AudioDevices.ForThisPlatform takes a microphone and a speaker by name: on Linux an ALSA device name such as pulse or plughw:CARD=MKII,DEV=0, on Windows part of the device's friendly name. ListMicrophones and ListSpeakers return the choices. The terminal client's Audio:Microphone and Audio:Speaker settings pass them on. On Linux, ALSA's default and pulse devices go through PipeWire's PulseAudio layer, which follows the PULSE_SOURCE and PULSE_SINK environment variables, so one process can be pointed at other PipeWire devices. Tests Uniform.Matrix.Audio.Tests runs mostly without devices: a tone through Opus keeps its pitch and level, a lost packet is concealed, a 44.1 kHz stereo microphone becomes 48 kHz mono frames, and queued frames reach the player unchanged. PipeWireTests goes through real ALSA and PipeWire with virtual devices it creates for itself with pactl load-module module-null-sink: a 500 Hz and a 1000 Hz tone played into a virtual microphone must come out of a virtual speaker, through the loopback, at their pitch and level. The variables above point the test's process at those devices. It removes the devices afterwards, and skips itself where no sound server runs, as on build servers. To see what such a test hears, record a virtual speaker with a short latency and interrupt the recorder rather than kill it; otherwise its last seconds stay unwritten. parecord --raw --latency-msec=20 --device=test_speaker.monitor --channels=1 --rate=48000 --format=s16le out.raw

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Calls/index..title: Uniform.Matrix.Calls | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Calls/index..summary: Uniform.Matrix.Calls Matrix 1:1 voice and video calls for the client engine, of two kinds: RtcCall: MatrixRTC through a LiveKit SFU, as Element X and Element Call make calls, over Uniform.LiveKit. LegacyCall: the m.call.* events of version 1, directly between the apps, as Element on the desktop and Element Classic make calls. Both are a VoiceCall, which the apps show the same way. Media goes over Uniform.Matrix.WebRtc, voice through Uniform.Matrix.Audio, and video is decoded with Uniform.Matrix.Video. Service CallService is a singleton beside the client engine. It follows SyncProcessor.Applied, routes each call event to its call, and raises IncomingCall for a fresh invite or ring to this user. It places MatrixRTC calls when the homeserver has a LiveKit transport, unless UseMatrixRtc is off, and legacy calls otherwise. Events go out through the OutboxSender, which encrypts them in encrypted rooms, as Element does. TURN credentials come from the homeserver's /voip/turnServer, and are kept until shortly before they expire. To add calls to an app, register the service, and set the devices when the app chooses them: builder.Services.AddSingleton<CallService>(); // … calls.Devices = () => AudioDevices.ForThisPlatform(microphone, speaker); calls.IncomingCall += call => ShowRinging(call); VoiceCall call = await calls.PlaceCallAsync(roomId); A MatrixRTC call Joining. An OpenID token buys a LiveKit token from the homeserver's authorization service at /sfu/get, so this side's identity on the SFU is @user:server:DEVICE. The call publishes on the SFU and writes its membership, the state event org.matrix.msc3401.call.member with state key _@user:server_DEVICE_m.call. A delayed event of empty content (MSC4140) ends the membership 18 seconds after the device stops restarting it, every 4 seconds. Ringing. The caller sends org.matrix.msc4075.rtc.notification with ring, referring to its membership. The callee rings while the caller is in the call, until it answers by joining, or declines with org.matrix.msc4310.rtc.decline. Connected. Once the peer's membership is there, each side sends its media key in io.element.call.encryption_keys to the peer's call devices over Olm, through CryptoService.SendEncryptedToDevicesAsync. Keys come back in ToDeviceReceived. In encrypted rooms, frames are encrypted as Element Call encrypts them. A peer on another homeserver is subscribed to on its own SFU, with a token of its service's /get_token. Reconnecting. After a network change, a lost signalling connection, or a media path down for 2 seconds, the call joins its SFU again with a new token. It publishes again and moves the media there, and the others' SFUs are joined again. The membership, the keys and the identity on the SFU stay, so the peer goes on decrypting. The call ends after 45 seconds without success. When the delayed leave was sent meanwhile, the membership is written again. LiveKit does not pass on the video orientation, so the camera is told to make its pictures Upright before encoding. When the homeserver's authorization service takes delayed leaves, as its delegate_delayed_leave tells, the call hands its leave over with a delay of an hour and restarts it itself only every 5 minutes, as Element Call does. The service sends it when this side drops off LiveKit. When the handover fails, the call keeps a short leave of its own. After reconnecting, a leave the service sent meanwhile is armed again, and the membership written again. Ended. Hanging up sends the delayed leave at once and leaves the SFUs. The call ends when the peer's membership goes, or on a decline or a timeout. A legacy call A LegacyCall: Ringing or inviting. The caller sends m.call.invite with the offer, and the callee rings until it answers, rejects, or the invite's lifetime passes. Connecting. The callee answers with m.call.answer; the caller picks the first answer with m.call.select_answer, so the user's other devices stop ringing. Candidates go both ways in m.call.candidates batches, ending with an empty candidate; those that arrive before the offer or answer wait for it. Connected. VoiceMedia sends the microphone as Opus, and plays what arrives through a jitter buffer, paced by the speaker. Muted stops sending. When the caller sends video, IsVideo is set while it rings, and the answer accepts the video, unless CallService.ReceiveVideo is off. VideoReceiver decodes it on its own task and the pictures come in PictureReceived. When decoding falls behind or a frame does not decode, frames are skipped up to a keyframe, which the peer is asked for. AnswerWithVideoAsync also sends this side's camera, from the platform's IVideoCamera in CallService.Camera: its encoded VP8 frames go to the peer once connected, and the peer's keyframe requests go to its encoder. PlaceVideoCallAsync calls with video. The camera's rotation goes with its frames, and its small Previewed pictures come in PreviewReceived; CameraOff pauses it, and SwitchCamera changes cameras. The peer's video is decoded by the platform's VideoDecoder, e.g. Android's hardware one, or by the C# decoder; a device that cannot keep up asks the sender for less, and for full quality again once it can. Ended. m.call.hangup from either side, m.call.reject, a timeout, or a failed connection; EndReason says which. Tests Uniform.Chat.Server.Tests calls over MatrixRTC between two client engines of a homeserver with LiveKit on, when LIVEKIT_SERVER names LiveKit's server program. It checks the ring, the answer, encrypted voice both ways, and a hangup that ends the call on both sides. Uniform.Matrix.Calls.Tests runs two legacy calls against each other in memory, with fake devices that record and play tones in real time: a call that each side must hear and then hang up, and a rejected call. Where Chromium is installed, it calls with a canvas as its camera, and the call must decode its pictures.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Client/index.title: Uniform.Matrix.Client | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Client/index.summary: Uniform.Matrix.Client The headless client. builder.AddMatrixClient() registers the Matrix and storage options, session logging under the data directory, storage, encryption, sync and the outbox; the application adds its own ICredentialPrompt for the first login. The data directory defaults to ~/.local/share/<app> by the host's application name. MatrixWorker (hosted service) ├─ ClientStore.MigrateAsync create or upgrade the SQLite schema ├─ ClientSession.ConnectAsync resume stored token, or log in and store it ├─ sync full-state sync from stored position, then SyncLoopAsync │ └─ SyncProcessor save events + position, apply to RoomStore, publish SyncChanges └─ OutboxSender.RunAsync send queued messages in order a frontend reads SyncChanges and queues messages via OutboxSender The client stores encryption state in its SQLite database (EfCryptoStore), with the 32-byte pickle key in crypto.key (mode 0600). SyncProcessor decrypts each sync before storing it and re-decrypts stored events when late keys arrive; OutboxSender encrypts for encrypted rooms after loading the full member list, and fails a message rather than sending it in the clear when encryption is unavailable. Files for encrypted rooms are encrypted and uploaded, then sent through the outbox; MediaCache decrypts them after the hash check, and the server is not asked for thumbnails of ciphertext. CryptoService backs up new room keys after each sync, and MainWindow.Security.cs holds the recovery and verification dialogs. Not yet covered Registration, refresh tokens, push rules, spaces and threads.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Client/local.title: Local storage | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Client/local.summary: Local storage Each account has its own directory, <data directory>/<localpart>_<server>/, holding client.db and media/. Tables: Table Contents Accounts Homeserver, device ID, access token and the last next_batch Events Every received timeline event as JSON, indexed by room and time; redactions strip stored content Outbox Messages written locally, with state Pending, Sent or Failed Media Downloaded files, stored under media/ Events and the sync position are saved in one transaction before the in-memory state changes, so a crash can at worst re-apply a sync; events are deduplicated by ID. On start, the first sync asks for full state from the stored position, which rebuilds room names and members in memory without losing messages.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Client/outbo.title: Outbox | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Client/outbo.summary: Outbox Messages are written to the Outbox table first and then sent in order. Each message gets its transaction ID when queued and keeps it across retries and restarts, so the server never stores a resent message twice. A transient failure (network, 5xx, rate limit) keeps the message and pauses the queue to keep order; a permanent rejection (e.g. not in the room) marks it Failed and moves on. If the app crashes after the server accepted a message but before it was marked Sent, its echo in sync carries the transaction ID and confirms it. SQLite is the default, through EF Core. No EF Core provider stores YAML, so a YAML store would be a separate implementation of ClientStore.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Client/rich-.title: Rich text | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Client/rich-.summary: Rich text MarkdownComposer turns typed Markdown into formatted_body with Markdig (CommonMark, strikethrough, autolinks, raw HTML disabled), unwraps a single paragraph like Element, and turns completed nicks into matrix.to mention pills; text without formatting or mentions is sent without HTML. HtmlText renders incoming HTML with AngleSharp into terminal text: blocks, lists, quotes, code, links with addresses, mention names, hidden spoilers, and no mx-reply fallback.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Client/room-.title: Room state | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Client/room-.summary: Room state RoomStore turns sync responses into one Room per room ID. Apply returns SyncChanges so a UI only redraws what changed. A room keeps: current state, with display name computed per spec: name, alias, then member names such as "Alice and Bob" or "Empty Room (was Alice)"; members, with display names disambiguated as "Bob (@bob:server)" while shared; the most recent MaxTimelineLength events, with redactions applied. A limited timeline clears older events, since they no longer connect; BackfillAsync loads history back; typing users, read receipts, unread counts, tags, fully read marker and the direct-message user from m.direct. Servers may lazy-load members, sending only those needed for the timeline. LoadMembersAsync fetches the full list, e.g. for a nick list. The store is not thread-safe; apply syncs and read rooms on one thread. Stored history The room state keeps only a recent timeline; the whole history that the client has seen is in the database, read a page of lines at a time. Each stored event has a line in display order. An event shown on its own gets a line from its time: its origin_server_ts × LinesPerMillisecond, plus a count of earlier events of the same millisecond. Edits, reactions and redactions take the line of the event they change, so a message always loads with all of its changes, however much later they came. A change that arrives before its target, e.g. a reaction to a message older than the stored history, waits without a line until that message is stored. GetRoomLinesAsync returns the newest lines before a given line; to show a room and scroll back: RoomLines newest = await store.GetRoomLinesAsync(roomId, 250); RoomLines older = await store.GetRoomLinesAsync(roomId, 100, newest.OldestLine); Lines from time keep their order when older history fills a gap after a limited sync.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Client/track.title: Track rooms | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Client/track.summary: Track rooms Room state is in the Uniform.Matrix.Client library (using Uniform.Matrix.Client.State;), which builds on the protocol client: RoomStore store = new(client.UserId!); await foreach (SyncResponse sync in client.SyncLoopAsync(since: store.NextBatch, cancellationToken: cancellationToken)) { SyncChanges changes = store.Apply(sync); foreach (Room room in changes.Invited) Console.WriteLine($"{room.InviterUserId} invited you to {room.DisplayName}"); foreach (TimelineBatch batch in changes.Timeline) { if (batch.Limited) Console.WriteLine($"[{batch.Room.DisplayName}] -- some messages skipped --"); foreach (ClientEvent clientEvent in batch.Events) { if (!clientEvent.TryGetContent(out MessageContent? message) || message.Body is null) continue; Console.WriteLine($"[{batch.Room.DisplayName}] <{batch.Room.GetMemberDisplayName(clientEvent.Sender)}> {message.Body}"); } } } Scroll back with await store.BackfillAsync(client, room), which prepends older events to room.Timeline until room.HasMoreHistory is false.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Gui.Terminal.title: Uniform.Matrix.Gui.Terminal | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Gui.Terminal.summary: Uniform.Matrix.Gui.Terminal Terminal.Gui components without Matrix types, for every terminal application: SettingsWindow lists a SettingsEditor's options with value, source and description, and edits, resets, applies, saves, loads and exports them. LogWindow lists session logs, filters entries by level and text, colors them by level, shows whole entries and follows the current file. Dialogs has the general prompts: ask, confirm, choose, pick one of a list, pick a file, show text or a value to copy. TextWrapper wraps text by terminal columns, so emoji and CJK take two.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Hosting/inde.title: Uniform.Matrix.Hosting | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Hosting/inde.summary: Uniform.Matrix.Hosting Settings and logging for any application on the .NET generic host, the client's and later the server's. Registered with builder.AddSettings(), builder.AddSessionLogging(directory, keep) and services.AddOptionSection<T>(configuration, section); folders follow the XDG base directories through AppDirectories. Settings SettingsStore adds two configuration layers: the application's settings file ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/<app>/settings.json, where <app> is the host's application name in kebab case, e.g. uniform-chat-terminal) right after appsettings.json, so environment and command line still win, and an in-memory applied layer on top. Applying sets the top layer and reloads the configuration; saving merges into the file, clears those keys from the applied layer and reloads. Options read through IOptionsMonitor<UiOptions> change at once; the others are marked [RestartRequired] and read at start. Each application registers its option records with AddOptionSection<T>, and OptionCatalog lists their properties by reflection, with descriptions read from the XML documentation of each record's assembly, so the settings window and the API reference say the same. [Secret] options are not shown, saved or exported. SettingsEditor holds the window's edits and is tested without the UI. Logs FileLoggerProvider writes logs/client-yyyyMMdd-HHmmss.log per session and prunes the oldest beyond Storage:LogFilesKept. LogFiles lists and parses them: a line with time and level starts an entry, other lines (stack traces) continue it.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Cli.title: Directories and account data | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Cli.summary: Directories and account data PublicRoomsResponse rooms = await client.GetPublicRoomsAsync(searchTerm: "dotnet", limit: 20); // like /list UserDirectoryResponse users = await client.SearchUsersAsync("bob"); string dmRoomId = await client.CreateDirectRoomAsync("@bob:matrix.org"); // also updates m.direct await client.SetTagAsync(roomId, RoomTags.Favourite); await client.IgnoreUserAsync("@spammer:example.org");

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Cli.title: Errors | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Cli.summary: Errors try { await client.JoinRoomAsync("#missing:matrix.org"); } catch (MatrixException ex) when (ex.Errcode == ErrorCodes.NotFound) { Console.Error.WriteLine("No such room"); } catch (MatrixException ex) when (ex.Errcode == ErrorCodes.Forbidden) { Console.Error.WriteLine($"Not allowed: {ex.Error}"); } MatrixException is thrown when the server returns a Matrix error body. Rate-limited requests are retried automatically before an exception is thrown, unless the server asks to wait longer than MaxRateLimitDelay (30 seconds); then ex.RetryAfter says how long to wait. Other failures, such as an HTML error page from a proxy, throw HttpRequestException with the HTTP status code.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Cli.title: Files and devices | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Cli.summary: Files and devices await using FileStream file = File.OpenRead("cat.png"); await client.SendFileAsync(roomId, file, "cat.png", "image/png"); // uploads, then sends m.image using MediaDownload media = await client.DownloadMediaAsync(MxcUri.Parse(message.Url!)); await using FileStream copy = File.Create(media.FileName ?? "download"); await media.Content.CopyToAsync(copy); IReadOnlyList<Device> devices = await client.GetDevicesAsync(); try { await client.DeleteDevicesAsync(["OLDDEVICE"], password: null); } catch (UserInteractiveAuthException ex) when (ex.AcceptsPassword) { await client.DeleteDevicesAsync(["OLDDEVICE"], AskPassword()); // answers the challenge }

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Cli.title: Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Client | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Cli.summary: Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Client MatrixClient wraps one homeserver and one session. It is split into partial files by spec area. Each endpoint is one method that sends a request and returns a response record. All requests go through a single private SendAsync, which: adds the bearer token for authenticated endpoints, and refuses to send if not logged in; serializes the body with MatrixJson.Options; retries rate-limited requests up to MaxRateLimitRetries times, waiting as long as the server asks, unless that is longer than MaxRateLimitDelay; turns other non-2xx responses into a MatrixException when the body is a standard error, or an HttpRequestException otherwise. Path segments such as room IDs (!abc:server), aliases (#room:server) and event IDs are always percent-escaped. The caller owns the HttpClient, which keeps the library usable with IHttpClientFactory, custom handlers and test stubs. Session After login, Session holds a MatrixSession with homeserver, user ID, device ID and access token. Store it and pass it to the MatrixClient(HttpClient, MatrixSession) constructor to resume without logging in again. Sync SyncLoopAsync is the main way to receive events. It long-polls sync, passes each next_batch as the next since, and yields every response. Transient failures (network errors, 5xx, timeouts, rate limiting) are retried with exponential backoff between SyncRetryDelay and SyncRetryMaxDelay; other errors, such as an expired token, end the loop with an exception. User-interactive auth Some endpoints, such as deleting devices, answer the first request with 401 and a body listing accepted auth flows and a session ID. Such bodies have no errcode, so the request pipeline maps them to UserInteractiveAuthException before ordinary Matrix errors. Methods that need it take a password and answer a m.login.password challenge themselves; without a password the exception reaches the caller, who can ask the user and call again. Discovery HomeserverDiscovery.DiscoverAsync follows server discovery: it reads https://{server}/.well-known/matrix/client and falls back to https://{server}/ when the file does not exist.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Cli.title: Log in | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Cli.summary: Log in using Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Client; using Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Core; using HttpClient http = new(); // Find the homeserver for the server part of the user ID UserId userId = UserId.Parse("@alice:matrix.org"); Uri homeserver = await HomeserverDiscovery.DiscoverAsync(http, userId.ServerName); MatrixClient client = new(http, homeserver); // Log in with a full user ID or a localpart await client.LoginWithPasswordAsync(userId.ToString(), password, deviceDisplayName: "My app"); Save client.Session to resume later without the password: MatrixClient resumed = new(http, storedSession); LogoutAsync invalidates the token and deletes the device.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Cli.title: Receive events | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Cli.summary: Receive events Filter filter = new() { Room = new RoomFilter { Timeline = new RoomEventFilter { Limit = 50, LazyLoadMembers = true } } }; string filterId = await client.CreateFilterAsync(filter); await foreach (SyncResponse sync in client.SyncLoopAsync(filter: filterId, onRetry: (exception, wait) => Console.Error.WriteLine($"Sync failed, retrying in {wait}: {exception.Message}"), cancellationToken: cancellationToken)) { foreach ((string roomId, JoinedRoom room) in sync.Rooms.Join) { foreach (ClientEvent clientEvent in room.Timeline.Events) { if (clientEvent.Type != EventTypes.RoomMessage) continue; if (!clientEvent.TryGetContent(out MessageContent? message)) continue; Console.WriteLine($"[{roomId}] {clientEvent.Sender}: {message.Body}"); } } foreach ((string roomId, InvitedRoom invite) in sync.Rooms.Invite) Console.WriteLine($"Invited to {roomId}"); } Store the last NextBatch together with the session and pass it as since to continue where you left off. When room.Timeline.Limited is true, the server skipped events. Fetch them with GetMessagesAsync starting from room.Timeline.PrevBatch.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Cli.title: Rooms and messages | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Cli.summary: Rooms and messages string roomId = await client.JoinRoomAsync("#general:matrix.org"); await client.SendTextAsync(roomId, "hello"); await client.SendEmoteAsync(roomId, "waves"); // * alice waves await client.SetRoomTopicAsync(roomId, "Friendly chat"); MessagesResponse page = await client.GetMessagesAsync(roomId, limit: 50); // newest first await client.SetReadMarkersAsync(roomId, page.Chunk[0].EventId, page.Chunk[0].EventId); await client.LeaveRoomAsync(roomId); Rich messages: await client.SendReplyAsync(roomId, originalEvent, "agreed"); // mentions the original sender await client.SendEditAsync(roomId, myEventId, "fixed typo"); await client.SendReactionAsync(roomId, eventId, "👍"); await client.SendHtmlAsync(roomId, "hi Bob", "hi Bob", new Mentions { UserIds = ["@bob:matrix.org"] }); Sends get a fresh transaction ID each time. To retry a send safely after a network error, pass the same transactionId again; the server then returns the original event instead of sending a duplicate.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Cor.title: Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Core | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Cor.summary: Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Core The types both sides of the protocol use: identifiers, events, the request and response records of the APIs, canonical JSON and error codes. Models are records with init properties. Responses mark spec-required fields required, so a response missing one fails during deserialization rather than surfacing as a null later. Collections default to empty, so sync.Rooms.Join never needs a null check. Events derive from MatrixEvent, which keeps content as raw JSON. TryGetContent reads it as a typed content record and returns false instead of throwing when another client sent malformed content. Content records such as MessageContent have no required members for the same reason. Constants for event types, message types, memberships and error codes live in static classes such as EventTypes and ErrorCodes. JSON names are mapped to snake_case by MatrixJson.Options; [JsonPropertyName] is only used for dotted keys such as m.relates_to and names that are not snake_case, such as displayname and msgtype. Links to rooms and users MatrixLink parses matrix.to links, matrix: URIs and bare identifiers into the target, an optional event and the via servers to join through. FindAll finds the links in a message body or its HTML, for example to offer joining a linked room. if (MatrixLink.TryParse("https://matrix.to/#/!abc:example.org?via=example.org", out MatrixLink? link)) await client.JoinRoomAsync(link.Target, link.Via);

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Cry.title: Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Crypto | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Cry.summary: Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Crypto End-to-end encryption is pure .NET, so the client runs on any platform .NET runs on, with no native libraries. Two layers: Olm and Megolm: a port of vodozemac 0.11.1, the maintained Rust implementation, to C#. It keeps vodozemac's API shape (OlmAccount, OlmSession, MegolmOutboundSession, MegolmInboundSession, Ed25519, PkEncryption, Sas) and its wire formats: Olm and Megolm messages with truncated MACs (session config version 1), libolm-compatible backup encryption, hkdf-hmac-sha256.v2 SAS MACs. X25519 and Ed25519 come from BouncyCastle; HKDF, HMAC, SHA-256 and AES from .NET. Errors are OlmException. The port keeps vodozemac's Apache-2.0 copyright notices; each ported file says so in its header, and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md at the repository root lists them. Pickles are vodozemac's own format, JSON encrypted with HKDF-derived AES-CBC and HMAC, so state written by the native library loads here and back. Libolm pickles and expanded Ed25519 keys are not supported. Unlike vodozemac, this code has not been audited, and the .NET runtime cannot guarantee constant-time execution or that secrets are wiped from memory; Dispose clears key buffers on a best-effort basis. OlmMachine: the Matrix protocol. Keys: signed device keys on first use, one-time keys topped up to half capacity from sync's device_one_time_keys_count, a fallback key replaced when used. Everything is signed over canonical JSON. Devices: /keys/query results are accepted only with a valid self-signature; a known device ID keeps its first fingerprint. Lists are marked outdated from device_lists.changed. Receiving: Olm to-device events are decrypted with an existing session or a new one from a pre-key message, and the payload must name us, our key and the actual sender. m.room_key becomes an inbound Megolm session; RoomKeyReceived lets callers retry waiting events. Megolm events are checked for the right room and against replayed indices. Sending: one outbound session per room, rotated after the room's message or time limit or when someone it was shared with left. The key goes to every device of every member over Olm, claiming and verifying one-time keys where no session exists. Our own copy is kept so our messages decrypt in sync. Cross-signing: /keys/query master, self-signing and user-signing keys are accepted only when the master key signed the others; devices note which self-signing key validly signed them. A device is cross-signed when that key belongs to a trusted identity: our own when its private master key is here, or verified by SAS; another user's when our user-signing key signed their master key. SetUpRecoveryAsync refuses to replace existing cross-signing keys, since that would distrust every device. Secret storage: m.secret_storage.v1.aes-hmac-sha2 (HKDF-SHA-256, AES-256-CTR, HMAC-SHA-256) with the key check from the key description, a base58 recovery key with prefix and parity, or a PBKDF2 passphrase. It holds the three cross-signing private keys and the backup key. Key backup: m.megolm_backup.v1.curve25519-aes-sha2. Sessions are exported from their first known index, encrypted to the backup's public key and uploaded in batches after each sync; BackedUp marks what is done. Uploads happen only with the private key of the current version, so a backup replaced on the server cannot capture keys. Restore imports sessions that reach further back than stored ones and raises RoomKeyReceived. Key requests: a missing session is requested once from our other devices with m.room_key_request. Requests and m.secret.request are answered only to our cross-signed or verified devices; forwarded keys and secrets are accepted only from them, only for our own outstanding requests, and secrets only when they match the published public keys. Verification: to-device SAS (m.sas.v1, curve25519-hkdf-sha256, hkdf-hmac-sha256.v2) with the accept commitment, emoji and decimals, and MACs over the device key and, when trusted, the master key. Afterwards our own device is signed with the self-signing key and asked for missing secrets; another user's master key is signed with the user-signing key. Imported sessions (backup, forwarded) are marked Imported, as their sender is not proven by Olm. All calls are serialized; state lives in an ICryptoStore as encrypted pickles. Private keys are stored as named values, encrypted with the pickle key. Encrypted attachments (EncryptedAttachments) use AES-256-CTR with a random key and an IV whose low 64 bits are zero, and SHA-256 of the ciphertext, which is checked before decrypting. The message carries file instead of url; MessageContent.MediaUrl gives either. Not yet covered QR code verification, in-room verification requests, dehydrated devices, and key export files.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Ser.title: Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Server | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Ser.summary: Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Server Pure protocol code of a homeserver, without storage: room versions 10, 11 and 12 (RoomVersion), the event format, content hashes, reference-hash event IDs, signing and redaction (EventFormat), the auth events selection and the authorization rules (AuthEvents, AuthRules), power levels, push rule evaluation (PushRules), signed requests between servers (FederationAuth), server names (ServerNames), room server ACLs (ServerAcl) and DNS SRV messages (DnsSrv). It is used by Uniform.Matrix.Server, and builds on Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Crypto for Ed25519 signatures. State resolution When a room's history forks, as when two servers send events at the same time, StateResolution.Resolve merges the states of the branches as the spec's state resolution v2 says, and with the v2.1 changes of room version 12. Keys every branch agrees on are kept. Conflicted power events (power levels, join rules, kicks and bans) are applied first, strongest sender first, each checked with AuthRules against what is resolved so far; the other conflicted events follow, ordered by the power levels they were sent under. The caller passes the events of the states and their auth chains: Dictionary<(string Type, string StateKey), string> merged = StateResolution.Resolve(RoomVersion.V12, [stateOfBranchA, stateOfBranchB], eventsById); AuthRules.CheckAuthChains checks received state, such as a joined room's, against each event's own auth events.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/event.title: Events and state | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/event.summary: Events and state EventSender turns an EventDraft into a PDU: it picks the auth events, prev_events (the room's forward extremities) and depth, hashes and signs it with the server's key (ServerKeys, in signing.key), computes the event ID, checks the authorization rules against the current state, and stores the event, its graph edges and the new state. Room state is stored as state groups: each state event makes a new group that records only its change against the previous group, with a full snapshot every 50 changes, so reading the state at any event is a short chain. StateCache keeps loaded groups, which never change. CurrentState has one row per type and state key for fast reads, with the membership of member events, so a user's rooms are one query. ClientFormat turns a stored PDU into the client format: no graph fields, unsigned with age, the transaction ID for the sending device, redacted_because and prev_content.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/feder.title: Federation | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/feder.summary: Federation Federation is being built, behind Federation:Enabled. In Federation/: ServerResolver finds other servers as the spec's server name resolution says: IP literals and names with a port directly, otherwise /.well-known/matrix/server delegation, then SRV records (_matrix-fed._tcp, then the deprecated _matrix._tcp), else port 8448. SrvLookup asks the system's name servers over UDP with the messages of DnsSrv; with an SRV record the connection goes to its target, while the Host header, and with it the TLS name, stays the server name. FederationClient sends requests signed with FederationAuth (in Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Server) as an X-Matrix authorization, through the same public-addresses-only handler as push gateways and URL previews. RemoteServerKeys fetches other servers' keys from their /_matrix/key/v2/server, else from the key servers of Federation:TrustedKeyServers (whose own signature is checked too), accepts them only when every listed key signed the answer, and keeps the answer in ServerKeyResponses until valid_until_ts, at most a week. Old keys count for signatures too, and when nothing can be fetched the last answer is used even when expired. /_matrix/key/v2/query answers as a key server, each answer countersigned. ServerAuthentication is middleware on endpoints marked RequireFederation(): it buffers the body, checks the signature over the raw request target, and gives the endpoint the origin with GetOrigin(). FederationEndpoints serves /_matrix/key/v2/server, /_matrix/federation/v1/version, query/profile, make_join, send_join (v2) and send, and ProfileService asks other servers for their users' profiles. Joins: RoomService.JoinAsync sends joins of room IDs of other servers that are not here to RemoteJoins, which asks the room's server for a make_join template, signs it, sends it with send_join, fetches the signing keys of every sending server at once (RemoteServerKeys.PrefetchAsync: the key servers first, in batches, then each server, 20 at a time, each waiting at most Federation:KeyRequestTimeout), checks the content hash and signature of every returned event and the auth rules against each event's own auth events (AuthRules.CheckAuthChains), drops the events that fail, as other servers do, and stores the room with EventSender.StoreJoinedRoomAsync. The returned state and auth chain get negative stream positions, so they sort as history before the join and never count as new. On the resident side EventSender.MakeMembershipAsync builds the template and AcceptMembershipAsync checks the signed join (its ID, hash, origin and the auth rules) before storing it like a local event. Transactions: /send hands each PDU to RemoteEvents, which first asks the sending server for up to 20 events missing before it (get_missing_events) and accepts them oldest first, then hands the PDU to EventSender.AcceptEventAsync, which runs the checks on receipt; see below. When previous or auth events are still missing after that, RemoteEvents asks for the state before the event with /state_ids, fetches the events of it that are not here with /event, and stores them as history. FederationSender follows ServerStream and hands local users' events, remote joins this server accepted, and local users' device changes (m.device_list_update) to FederationQueue. The queue keeps one batch per destination (up to 50 PDUs and 100 EDUs per transaction) and retries failures with pauses doubling from 2 seconds to 5 minutes; a 4xx refusal other than 429 drops the batch. PDUs and the EDUs that matter later are also kept in the FederationOutbox table until sent, and FederationQueue.ResumeAsync queues them again at start; typing and presence stay in memory. RemoteActivity sends and receives typing (m.typing) and public read receipts (m.receipt); RemoteDevices handles keys across servers (user/keys/query, user/keys/claim, user/devices) and to-device messages (m.direct_to_device). Presence is not shared between servers yet. Invites of other servers' users: RemoteInvites signs the invite with EventSender.SignAsync (built and checked, not stored), sends it with invite v2 and the stripped room state from EventSender.InviteRoomStateAsync, checks that the invitee's server signed the same event, and stores it through AcceptEventAsync. Receiving invites is not there yet. Joins and leaves of other servers' users go through EventSender.MakeMembershipAsync and AcceptMembershipAsync; RemoteJoins.RejectInviteAsync rejects an invite to a room not here through the inviting server. RemoteJoins.ResolveAliasAsync asks query/directory for aliases of other servers. RoomHistory answers get_missing_events, backfill, event, state and state_ids for servers with a member in the room. Presence of local users goes out as m.presence EDUs from FederationSender; PresenceService.SetRemoteAsync keeps remote users' presence, which their server ends. Version 12 rooms are created by EventSender.CreateHashedRoomAsync, which signs the create event before the room row exists, as the room ID is its hash. Version 12 is the default for new rooms. Their IDs name no server, so joining one by ID needs via servers, which both clients send. Sliding sync (SlidingSyncService, POST /_matrix/client/unstable/org.matrix.simplified_msc3575/sync) builds rooms with SyncService, from the start for rooms a connection has not had and since its position for the others, and reshapes them into lists, room subscriptions and the to-device, e2ee, account data, receipts and typing extensions. Connections live in memory; an unknown position gets M_UNKNOWN_POS. Server:TrustedProxies turns on ASP.NET Core's forwarded headers for those addresses only. Room summaries (/v1/room_summary and the unstable im.nheko.summary paths) and space hierarchies (/v1/rooms/{roomId}/hierarchy, and /_matrix/federation/v1/hierarchy for other servers; rooms not here are asked from servers in them, the via servers a client gives, the alias's servers or the room ID's server, through federation hierarchy) come from DirectoryService, shown to members and invitees, and to anyone for public, knockable or world-readable rooms. SyncService answers /v1/rooms/{roomId}/relations (found by the related event's ID in the stored JSON, then checked), /v1/rooms/{roomId}/threads and timestamp_to_event; relations are also kept in the EventRelations table, from which thread roots get their m.thread summary in unsigned. Reports of content, rooms and users are kept by ReportService for the dashboard's review list, and logged. Media of other servers: MediaService fetches it on first use with FederationClient.DownloadAsync from /_matrix/federation/v1/media/download (a multipart/mixed answer: metadata, then the file; redirects to elsewhere are not followed), falling back to the legacy unsigned /_matrix/media/v3/download of older servers, and keeps it under an ID of its own in RemoteMedia; thumbnails of it are made here. The federation media endpoints serve local media the same way. The unauthenticated legacy reads, when turned on, serve local media only, so nobody without an account can make the server fetch from others. FederationSender keeps how far it got in FederationProgress, so events stored just before a stop are still sent after the restart. Older clients use r0 paths and unstable key backup and cross-signing paths; LegacyPaths maps them to v3 before routing. Requests no endpoint knows are logged with method and path, without the query. Room version 12 (RoomVersion.V12, RoomIdIsCreateHash): the room ID is ! and the create event's hash, the create event has no room_id and is left out of auth_events, and the creators (the sender and additional_creators, see AuthRules.Creators) have unlimited power and cannot be listed in power levels. Such rooms can be joined through via servers, since their IDs name no server; creating them here is refused until room creation builds the create event before the room's row. FederationTests run two servers in memory whose federation clients reach each other through a test handler. HTTPS comes from TlsCertificate (in Http/), which reads the PEM files of Tls:*, sends the intermediates with the certificate (other servers check the chain) and reads the files again within a minute of a renewal. Receiving events, forks and state resolution EventSender.AcceptEventAsync (in EventSender.Remote.cs) checks a received event in the spec's order: Its content hash, and the sender server's signature. Its own auth events: all stored here, of this room, each once, and of the kinds its type needs; the auth rules must allow it against them. The state before it: the state after each of its previous events, merged when they differ, with the state its server reported for previous events not here. The auth rules must allow it against that state. Events failing 1–3 are rejected and not stored. The room's current state: when that no longer allows the event, as when its sender was banned meanwhile on another server, the event is stored soft-failed. Soft-failed events stay in the room graph but are not shown and not built on; a global query filter on EventRow.SoftFailed hides them, and the few queries that need them ignore it. Each event keeps the state groups before and after it (StateGroupBefore, StateGroup); /state_ids answers with the state before, as other servers expect. When the room has several forward extremities, its current state is merged from their states by StateResolution in Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Server. Sync sends state that changed without the timeline showing it, as after such a merge, in the room's state. Room ACLs (m.room.server_acl) are checked by RoomAcls for the requesting server: joins, leaves, invites and history are refused, and its events, typing and receipts in /send are dropped for rooms whose ACL denies it.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/index.title: Uniform.Matrix.Server | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/index.summary: Uniform.Matrix.Server The homeserver is three projects: Project Role Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Server Pure protocol code, no storage: room versions 10, 11 and 12, the event format, content hashes, reference-hash event IDs, signing, redaction and the authorization rules. Uniform.Matrix.Server The engine: builder.AddMatrixServer() registers options, the database and services; app.MapMatrixServer() adds the middleware and maps the endpoints. Uniform.Chat.Server The application: reads settings, sets up logging, and runs with the Terminal.Gui dashboard or without it (Host:Ui). WebApplicationBuilder builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args); builder.AddSettings(); builder.AddMatrixServer(); WebApplication app = builder.Build(); app.MapMatrixServer(); await app.RunAsync(); Not yet covered Room upgrades, search, partial-state joins of large rooms, email pushers (stored but not sent), and PostgreSQL.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/prese.title: Presence | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/prese.summary: Presence PresenceService keeps presence in memory, like typing: each change takes a ServerStream position, and sync sends m.presence for the user and everyone sharing a joined room with them. A sync marks the user online, or idle with set_presence=unavailable; set_presence=offline changes nothing. A state chosen with the presence API, such as unavailable or offline to appear away, is not changed by syncing. A timer takes users offline once they have not synced for PresenceService.OfflineAfter (2 minutes), which wakes the syncs of the people who see them. Presence is lost on restart. The server never sees private keys. It checks that uploaded device keys, cross-signing keys and signatures are signed as the spec requires, hands out each one-time key once, and stores encrypted backups as they come.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/push..title: Push rules and pushers | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/push..summary: Push rules and pushers Push rules and unread counts Each user's push rules are stored as the m.push_rules account data that clients sync, and changed through /pushrules. PushRuleService merges them with PushRules.Defaults (in Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Server) on every read: a stored default rule keeps only its enabled and actions, so changes to the defaults reach users who customised their rules. User rules come before the defaults of their kind, except that .m.rule.master stays first. Initial syncs always carry m.push_rules, also for users who never changed a rule. notification_count and highlight_count in sync are worked out when the sync is built, not stored per event: the room's events by others after the user's read receipt (or their own latest event, whichever is later) go through PushRules.Evaluate, newest first and at most PushRuleService.MaxCounted of them. The evaluator implements the condition kinds of the spec (event_match with globs and word boundaries for content.body, event_property_is, event_property_contains, contains_display_name, room_member_count, sender_notification_permission) and skips the deprecated name-based mention rules for events with m.mentions. Encrypted messages count through .m.rule.encrypted, but the server cannot see mentions inside them; clients highlight those themselves. Pushers Pushers say where a user's notifications go, usually a push gateway that wakes a phone app. PusherService keeps them in the Pushers table; each belongs to the device that set it and goes when that device logs out. PushNotifier is a background service that follows ServerStream: for each new event it runs the push rules of the room's joined members (and of the invitee of an invite) with PushRuleService.DecideAsync, and posts a notification in the push gateway API format to each of their http pushers, with the tweaks of the deciding rule and the user's unread count across rooms. The event_id_only format leaves out the content and names. Push keys the gateway rejects are deleted; failing gateways are logged and skipped. Events from before the server started are not pushed. Gateway URLs come from users, so the gateway client (PushNotifier.CreateHandler) connects only to public addresses unless Push:AllowPrivateGateways is on. It checks the very addresses it connects to, in SocketsHttpHandler.ConnectCallback, so a host name cannot resolve to a public address for a check and a private one for the request.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/rate-.title: Rate limits | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/rate-.summary: Rate limits RateLimits.AddMatrixRateLimits (in Http/) sets up ASP.NET Core's rate limiter with two token-bucket policies, which endpoints opt into with RequireRateLimiting: RateLimits.Writes per access token, on room creation, invites, sending, state, redactions and uploads; and RateLimits.Logins per client address, on /login and /register. A refused request gets 429 with M_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, retry_after_ms and a Retry-After header; MatrixClient waits that long and retries. The RateLimits:* settings are read at startup. Reads and sync are not limited. Client addresses come from the connection, as forwarded headers are not read yet, so behind a reverse proxy the login limits are shared by all users.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/reque.title: Requests | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/reque.summary: Requests ASP.NET Core minimal APIs, one Map… extension per spec area in Endpoints/. Each endpoint reads the request, calls a service and returns JSON. MatrixHttp.HandleAsync wraps every request: CORS headers, and standard errors from exceptions. A MatrixException becomes its status and errcode; MatrixErrorException adds fields such as current_version; AuthenticationRequiredException answers 401 with the user-interactive auth flows; bad JSON becomes M_BAD_JSON or M_NOT_JSON; unknown paths M_UNRECOGNIZED. RequireAccessToken() on a route group checks the token from the Authorization header (or the deprecated access_token query parameter); handlers get the user with http.GetRequester(), or http.GetOwnRequester(userId) for endpoints that take a user ID and must refuse other users. The Requester carries the account's admin, suspended and locked flags. A locked account is refused with M_USER_LOCKED and soft_logout on every request but logging out. RejectSuspended() refuses suspended accounts with M_USER_SUSPENDED on sending, joining, inviting, creating rooms, profile changes and uploads. RequireAdmin() guards AdminEndpoints, which serve the spec's whois, suspend and lock and a subset of Synapse's admin API at its paths. Requests through the local admin socket need no access token: AdminSocket marks the socket's connections, and they act as an admin without an account. File permissions decide who may open the socket. ManagementEndpoints answer only there, for uniform-chat-server manage: the status with the counters and the server's files, and the settings, read with their sources, applied live and saved by the server. They take known options that are not secret, with valid values; elsewhere they answer as unknown. Access tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes, so a leaked database does not leak sessions.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/servi.title: Services | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/servi.summary: Services Folder Services Accounts/ AccountService (register, log in, devices, passwords), UserInteractiveAuth, AccountDataService (account data and tags), PushRuleService (push rules and unread counts), PusherService and PushNotifier (pushers and push gateways), ProfileService, PresenceService, AdminService (the dashboard's user and room windows, and the remote admin API: whois, suspension, locks, room shutdown, media), RegistrationTokens (configured and stored tokens, with uses and expiry), ServerNotices (notices rooms of the notices account) Rooms/ RoomService (create, join, invite, leave, state, redact, read), EventSender, ReceiptService, TypingService (in memory), DirectoryService (aliases, public rooms, user search) Sync/ SyncService, ServerStream, SyncFilter, Visibility Encryption/ DeviceKeyService (device, one-time, fallback and cross-signing keys, signatures), ToDeviceService (to-device messages and device lists), KeyBackupService Media/ UrlPreviewService (page previews), MediaService (files under media/ in the data directory; media reserved with /media/v1/create is a row with an empty content type until its file arrives, and downloads wait for it up to timeout_ms), Thumbnailer

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/stora.title: Storage | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/stora.summary: Storage EF Core on SQLite, ServerDbContext with entities in Storage/Entities.cs. DatabaseMigrator applies migrations at start, before the server answers. Each schema change adds a migration: dotnet tool run dotnet-ef migrations add <Name> --project src/Uniform.Matrix.Server --output-dir Storage/Migrations Services take an IDbContextFactory<ServerDbContext> and use a short-lived context per operation; they are singletons.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/sync..title: Sync and the stream | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/sync..summary: Sync and the stream ServerStream is one counter for every change a sync must notice: events, account data, receipts, typing, device list changes and to-device messages. WriteAsync(position => …) runs a change with the next position, one at a time, so positions commit in order, and wakes waiting syncs. Sync tokens are s and a position; /messages and prev_batch use the same tokens. Changes that are not stored, such as typing, still take a position, and the counter itself is stored, so positions are never reused after a restart. SyncService builds a response for the positions after the token: joined rooms with their timeline, state and summary, invites with stripped state, left rooms, account data, receipts and typing, to-device messages, device list changes and key counts. Incremental syncs long-poll with ServerStream.WaitPastAsync until something reaches the user. Visibility applies history visibility to every event a user is shown, and SyncFilter the parts of filters the server applies.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/testi.title: Testing | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/testi.summary: Testing Uniform.Matrix.Server.Tests start the whole server in memory with TestHomeserver (ASP.NET Core's test server, a temporary data directory) and drive it with our own MatrixClient. Server logs go to the test output. EncryptionTests run two of our OlmMachines against it: messages between users, recovery from backup, key forwarding and emoji verification. await using TestHomeserver server = await TestHomeserver.StartAsync(new Dictionary<string, string?> { ["Server:Registration"] = "Open" }); MatrixClient alice = server.CreateClient(); await alice.RegisterAsync("alice", "password"); string roomId = await alice.CreateRoomAsync(new CreateRoomRequest { Name = "Kitchen" });
