Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/url-p.title: URL previews | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Server/url-p.summary: URL previews UrlPreviewService answers preview_url when UrlPreviews:Enabled is on: it fetches the page, reads its OpenGraph og: tags with AngleSharp (the page's <title> and description when there are none), fetches og:image and stores it as media of the user who asked, and returns it as an mxc:// URI with matrix:image:size. A link to an image previews as that image. Pages and images are read up to UrlPreviews:MaxSize within UrlPreviews:Timeout, and results are cached per address for UrlPreviews:CacheDuration. The HTTP client is the same kind as for push gateways (PublicAddresses.CreateHandler): only public addresses, checked on every connection including redirects, unless UrlPreviews:AllowPrivateAddresses is on.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Video/index..title: Uniform.Matrix.Video | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.Video/index..summary: Uniform.Matrix.Video Video for calls, in pure C# with no native libraries: a VP8 decoder that turns the frames of a video call into pictures, and a VP8 encoder that makes frames of pictures. Nothing here knows about Matrix or the network: Uniform.Matrix.WebRtc puts the frames together from RTP, and Uniform.Matrix.Calls decodes them and gives the pictures to the app. Decoding Vp8Decoder decodes one frame at a time, in order, starting with a keyframe. Decode returns the picture of a shown frame, or null for a frame kept only as a reference, such as an alternate reference frame. A frame that cannot be decoded throws InvalidDataException; after that the decoder waits for the next keyframe. To decode a stream frame by frame: Vp8Decoder decoder = new(); foreach (byte[] frame in frames) { if (decoder.Decode(frame) is VideoFrame picture) Show(picture); } A VideoFrame is I420: full-size luma, and both chroma planes at half the width and height, rounded up, each tightly packed. CopyToBgra converts it to 32-bit BGRA for display, from the BT.601 limited range that WebRTC video uses; e.g. into a bitmap's rows: picture.CopyToBgra(pixels, stride); Encoding Vp8Encoder encodes pictures as VP8 frames, in pure C# too. A keyframe predicts each macroblock from its edges by DC; the inter frames between keyframes predict each from the previous picture at the same place, and skip those with nothing left to code, which for a camera is most of the picture. Residuals are transformed and quantized with one quantizer, and written with the default probabilities, without a loop filter. A keyframe comes every KeyframeInterval frames, and after RequestKeyframe, e.g. when the peer lost packets. Quantizer, 0 to 127, trades size for quality. The encoder reconstructs each frame with the decoder's own inverse transforms, so Reconstruction is the picture that decoders show; the tests check that bit for bit, and that Chromium decodes the frames. To encode a picture and send it in a call: Vp8Encoder encoder = new(quantizer: 40); await connection.SendVideoAsync(encoder.Encode(picture)); With MotionSearch, on by default, an inter macroblock may predict from a moved place: the neighbours' vectors and a diamond search of even whole pixels inside the frame are tried, and a vector is taken when it saves more than its bits. Even whole pixels keep chroma on whole pixels too, so predictions are plain copies. How the decoder is built The decoder is a port of the reference decoder in RFC 6386, Attachment One, with arrays and indices in place of pointers. Its constant tables in Vp8Tables.cs are generated from the reference sources. It works as the reference does, one macroblock row at a time: Modes and motion vectors, from the first partition. Coefficients, from the row's partition, dequantized. Prediction, intra or from a reference frame with the six-tap filter, plus the inverse transforms of the residual. The loop filter, one row behind, so that intra prediction sees unfiltered neighbours. Where the reference decoder and libvpx differ, it follows libvpx, which produced the test vectors' checksums. The tests decode all 17 VP8 test vectors of libvpx and compare the MD5 of every frame. The licence of the reference decoder and the test vectors is in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md. On a desktop computer it decodes about 150 to 250 frames a second at 640×480.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.WebRtc/index.title: Uniform.Matrix.WebRtc | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Matrix.WebRtc/index.summary: Uniform.Matrix.WebRtc The subset of WebRTC that a 1:1 call needs, in C#: one Opus audio stream each way, and VP8 video each way, interoperating with browsers, Element and LiveKit's SFU. Only DTLS uses a library, BouncyCastle; the rest is written here against the RFCs and their test vectors. Nothing here knows about Matrix; Uniform.Matrix.Calls builds calls on it. Layers STUN and TURN come from Uniform.Stun: StunClient transactions and the TurnClient, on the messages of Uniform.Stun.Protocol. Folder What Specification Ice/ IceAgent: host, server-reflexive and relayed candidates, connectivity checks, role conflicts, nomination, peer-reflexive candidates, consent; IceCandidate as SDP writes it RFC 8445, RFC 8839, RFC 7675 Dtls/ DtlsSrtp: DTLS 1.2 with BouncyCastle, use_srtp, the peer's certificate checked against its fingerprint, keys exported; DtlsCertificate self-signed ECDSA RFC 5764 Srtp/ SrtpSession: SRTP and SRTCP with AES_CM_128_HMAC_SHA1_80, rollover counters, replay windows RFC 3711 Rtp/ RtpPacket and JitterBuffer; VP8 frames put together by Vp8Depacketizer and split by Vp8Packetizer; receiver reports and picture loss indications of Rtcp, counted by ReceiverStatistics RFC 3550, RFC 7741, RFC 4585 Sdp/ SessionDescription, and AudioSdp offers and answers: bundled, RTCP multiplexed, other media rejected RFC 8866, RFC 8829 One UDP socket carries everything. Its datagrams are told apart by their first byte, as RFC 7983 says: STUN 0–3, DTLS 20–63, TURN channel data 64–79, and RTP and RTCP 128–191. A connection AudioPeerConnection puts the layers together. The caller makes an offer, the callee answers, both trickle their candidates to the other, and both connect. The offerer controls ICE, and the answerer is the DTLS client, as browsers do. The following shows both sides in one process; in a call, the strings travel in Matrix events: await using AudioPeerConnection caller = new(), callee = new(); caller.CandidateGathered += candidate => callee.AddRemoteCandidate(candidate.ToString()); callee.CandidateGathered += candidate => caller.AddRemoteCandidate(candidate.ToString()); callee.AudioReceived += packet => Play(decoder.Decode(packet.Payload)); string answer = callee.AcceptOffer(caller.CreateOffer()); caller.AcceptAnswer(answer); await Task.WhenAll(caller.ConnectAsync(), callee.ConnectAsync()); await caller.SendAudioAsync(encoder.Encode(frame)); The voice and video pipelines see a connection as an IMediaConnection, so they also run over the connections of an SFU call together, such as LiveKitMedia. TURN servers, e.g. those of a homeserver's /voip/turnServer, go in PeerConnectionOptions.Servers; RelayOnly keeps the call on the relay, so the peer does not learn this device's addresses. Received video With PeerConnectionOptions.ReceiveVideo, an answer accepts the VP8 video of the peer's offer as recvonly, bundled with the audio; ReceivesVideo tells whether it did. The packets are put together into whole frames, given in order in VideoReceived, for a decoder such as that of Uniform.Matrix.Video. A frame waits for packets that come out of order. After a packet is lost, only a keyframe is given, and the connection asks the peer for one with an RTCP picture loss indication; RequestKeyframeAsync asks for one too, e.g. when a frame did not decode. Receiver reports go to the peer every second, so it can see the loss and the round trip. Sent video With PeerConnectionOptions.SendVideo, an answer also sends video when the peer's offer receives it; the section names this side's video SSRC and stream, so browsers make a track of it. SendVideoAsync takes encoded VP8 frames, e.g. from a hardware encoder, and sends each in RTP packets of at most 1100 bytes, timed by a 90 kHz clock from the moment of sending. When the peer asks for a keyframe, with a picture loss indication or a full intra request, KeyframeRequested tells the encoder. A call's caller offers video with CreateOffer(video: true): both ways, and the answer decides which ways it goes. SFUs An SFU, such as LiveKit, needs a few more things of a connection: Publishing: with SendOnly, an offer only sends, and AudioTrackId and VideoTrackId name the tracks in their msid, as the SFU was told of them. Subscribing: the SFU's offer may carry no audio before anyone publishes, and a data channel section, which is rejected. The transport connects all the same, its credentials at the session level when every section is rejected. Later offers on the same transport add the tracks. Sections an SFU left inactive come after active ones. ICE lite: an SFU that is an ICE lite agent makes this side control ICE, also when it answers. Streams: Vp8EncodedFrame.Ssrc tells the SFU's streams apart. Loss, bitrate and orientation Lost packets: the last 512 video packets sent are kept, and sent again, as sent, when the peer asks with a generic NACK, RFC 4585 6.2.1. A gap in the received video is asked for at once, before its frames wait for a keyframe. Bitrate: each receiver report carries a REMB with what the peer may send: the loss-based estimate of BandwidthEstimator, down on heavy loss and slowly up on little, within the cap of RequestBitrateAsync, e.g. when this device cannot decode more. The peer's REMBs, also Chromium's estimates as we announce goog-remb, come in BitrateRequested for the encoder. Sender reports: each second, a sender report of the video and one of the audio sent pair the wall-clock time with each stream's RTP time, so the peer can line picture and sound up, and carry the counts sent. Orientation: the 3GPP video orientation header extension, urn:3gpp:video-orientation, is offered and answered; a sent frame's rotation goes on its last packet, and a received frame's comes with it in Vp8EncodedFrame.Rotation. LiveKit does not answer it, so over LiveKit the rotation does not travel; SendsOrientation tells, and the sender turns its pictures upright itself, with VideoFrame.Rotated. Not supported: IPv6 and TCP candidates, mDNS host names (browsers' hidden host candidates; the peer-reflexive path covers them), renegotiation other than ICE restarts, lining up received video with audio, RTX retransmission streams, and transport-wide congestion control. Tests Uniform.Matrix.WebRtc.Tests checks each layer: STUN against the vectors of RFC 5769, and SRTP against those of RFC 3711 and libsrtp; TURN against an in-process fake server, and against a real one when UNIFORM_MATRIX_TURN (host:port) and UNIFORM_MATRIX_TURN_SECRET (the shared secret) are set; ICE between two agents directly, with a role conflict, and through two fake TURN servers; DTLS between two sides in memory; a whole call with headless Chromium's WebRTC, driven over the DevTools protocol, when Chromium is installed: each side must decode the other's tone.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Stun.Hosting/index..title: Uniform.Stun.Hosting | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Stun.Hosting/index..summary: Uniform.Stun.Hosting AddTurnServer binds TurnOptions to section Turn, lists it among the settings with AddOptionSection, and runs TurnServerHost as a hosted service. Every setting is restart-required, as the server binds its ports at start; the secrets are marked secret, so the settings windows neither show nor save them. The host makes the server's options from the settings: it resolves a host name in ExternalAddress, reads the TLS certificate with PemCertificate, which reads it again when a file changes, and combines the credentials of SharedSecrets, Users and every ITurnAuthenticator in the host. Settings that cannot work are logged and kept in Error, and the host runs on without the server, so a homeserver is not stopped by its TURN settings; Uniform.Stun.Server exits with that message instead. Uniform.Chat.Server embeds it: EmbeddedTurn registers an authenticator of the homeserver's Calls:TurnSharedSecret, or of a random secret of the run when that is not set, and sets Calls:TurnUris to the server's own addresses.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Stun.Protocol/index.title: Uniform.Stun.Protocol | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Stun.Protocol/index.summary: Uniform.Stun.Protocol STUN and TURN messages without sockets, shared by the clients of Uniform.Stun, the server of Uniform.Turn, and the homeserver, which hands out TURN credentials. Type What Specification StunMessage Parse and encode messages; MESSAGE-INTEGRITY, FINGERPRINT and long-term keys RFC 8489 StunAttributeTypes, StunErrorCodes Attribute types and error codes of STUN, TURN and ICE RFC 8489, RFC 8656, RFC 8445 StunAddress XOR'ed address attributes RFC 8489 ChannelData TURN channel data, and framing of STUN and channel data on TCP and TLS streams RFC 8656 TurnCredentials Time-limited credentials from a shared secret, as homeservers and coturn's use-auth-secret use TURN REST API draft The cryptography is .NET's own: HMAC-SHA1 for integrity, MD5 for long-term keys, and a table-driven CRC-32 for fingerprints.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Stun.Server/index.h.title: Uniform.Stun.Server | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Stun.Server/index.h.summary: Uniform.Stun.Server The standalone STUN and TURN server, uniform-stun-server: a .NET host with AddSettings, one log file per session and the console, and AddTurnServer. Its appsettings.json turns the server on. When it cannot start, it prints why and where the settings are, and exits with 1. Its settings and data folders are named after the application, ~/.config/uniform-stun-server and ~/.local/share/uniform-stun-server. How to run it is in its user guide.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Stun/index.html.title: Uniform.Stun | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Stun/index.html.summary: Uniform.Stun STUN and TURN clients on a UDP socket that the caller owns and reads, as ICE shares one socket for everything: the caller gives STUN responses to StunClient.Receive and relayed data to TurnClient.TryUnwrap. StunClient: transactions with the retransmissions of RFC 8489. TurnClient: allocation with long-term credentials and their 401 and 438 challenges, permissions, channels, Send and Data indications, and refreshes until disposed or expired. Uniform.Matrix.WebRtc uses both for ICE. Over TCP or TLS, the caller frames the stream with ChannelData.FrameLength and pads channel data, as the Uniform.Turn tests do.

Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Turn/index.html.title: Uniform.Turn | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/Uniform.Turn/index.html.summary: Uniform.Turn A STUN and TURN server: TurnServer answers Binding requests and relays UDP for authenticated clients that reach it over UDP, TCP or TLS, following RFC 8656. Uniform.Stun.Hosting runs it in a .NET host. Requests Method Does Binding Answers the client's address, without credentials Allocate A relay socket on a random free port of the relay range, for UDP over IPv4; a retransmission gets the same answer, another request on the same 5-tuple 437 Refresh A new lifetime, from the default to the maximum; zero ends the allocation CreatePermission Lets the peers' addresses through for five minutes, all or none ChannelBind A channel for a peer for ten minutes; a channel has one peer and a peer one channel Send indication, channel data Data to a permitted peer Data from peers goes to the client on the peer's channel when bound, else in a Data indication; without a permission it is dropped. Over TCP and TLS, the server frames the stream with ChannelData.FrameLength and pads channel data; the allocation ends with the connection. Credentials Requests other than Binding need long-term credentials. An ITurnAuthenticator gives the keys a user may have: SharedSecretAuthenticator for time-limited credentials of shared secrets, StaticUserAuthenticator for fixed users, and CombinedAuthenticator for several. A request is accepted when its MESSAGE-INTEGRITY matches any key. Nonces are stateless: the time they were made and an HMAC of it with the client's address, under a key made at each start. They are stale after NonceLifetime, and a restart makes all stale, which clients answer by retrying with the new nonce. Safety DeniedPeers, by default IpRange.NonPublic, are refused with 403, so the server cannot be used to reach its own network; AllowedPeers make exceptions. The server's own relayed addresses are always allowed. Quotas per user name and in total (486 and 508), and lifetimes; a sweep every five seconds removes what has expired. Requests with comprehension-required attributes it does not know get 420, e.g. EVEN-PORT and RESERVATION-TOKEN, which it does not implement. Several networks UDP replies must leave from the address their request came to, or the client drops them. A socket on 0.0.0.0 leaves the choice to routing, which on a computer with several networks may pick another, e.g. the default route of a wired network while forwarded traffic arrives over WiFi. With ListenAddress 0.0.0.0, the server therefore binds a UDP socket on each IPv4 address of the interfaces that are up at start, and each relay socket on the address its client reached. TCP connections keep their addresses, so TCP listens on 0.0.0.0. The server checks its addresses every AddressCheckInterval and when NetworkChange.NetworkAddressChanged fires: it binds UDP on addresses that appeared, closes it on those that went, and ends the allocations on them, whose clients allocate again. Changing public address ExternalAddressSource is asked at start and at each check; Uniform.Stun.Hosting makes one that resolves a host name, or asks a STUN server with StunDiscovery. When the answer differs, new allocations get it. Existing ones keep their relayed address, and data to them is still delivered inside the server; their clients reach the server at the old address, which no longer leads there, so they end unrefreshed. Relaying inside the server Data from one allocation to another relayed address of the same server goes from one to the other in memory, without leaving the server. Two clients behind the same router as the server, e.g. at home, then need no NAT hairpinning, which many routers lack. Not implemented TCP relaying (RFC 6062), IPv6 relayed addresses, EVEN-PORT and reservations, the SHA-256 integrity of RFC 8489, and DTLS as a client transport. Browsers and the apps of this project use none of them for calls.

Uniform.Chat/building.html.title: Building | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/building.html.summary: Building dotnet build Every library generates its XML documentation file, so public members without doc comments show up as build warnings. The desktop and Android apps have their own notes: Uniform.Chat.Desktop and Uniform.Chat.Android. Releasing Pushing a version tag runs .github/workflows/release.yml: git tag v0.1.0 git push origin v0.1.0 The workflow builds and tests, packs the Uniform.Matrix.*, Uniform.Stun.*, Uniform.LiveKit.* and Uniform.Turn libraries with the tag's version, publishes the desktop app, the terminal client, the server, the STUN and TURN server and the MatrixRTC authorization server, each with its user guide, for linux-x64, linux-arm64, win-x64 and win-arm64 as self-contained single-file apps (.tar.gz for Linux, .zip for Windows), pushes the packages to NuGet.org, and creates a GitHub release with the archives, the signed Android APK uniform-chat-android-<version>.apk and SHA256SUMS.txt. A tag with a suffix, such as v0.2.0-alpha.1, makes a prerelease on both. Packages are pushed with trusted publishing: the job exchanges GitHub's OIDC token for a short-lived NuGet API key, so no key is stored. It needs a trusted publishing policy on nuget.org for this repository and release.yml, a release environment in the repository settings, and the nuget.org user name in the NUGET_USER secret. Android release signing The APK is signed with the app's release key, which Android uses to allow updates: an update signed with another key does not install over the app. Keep the keystore and its passwords safe and backed up; a lost key means users have to uninstall to get updates. Create the keystore once, outside the repository; keytool asks for the passwords: keytool -genkeypair -keystore ~/uniform-chat-release.keystore -alias uniform-chat -keyalg RSA -keysize 4096 -validity 10000 -dname "CN=Uniform Chat" Then add these repository secrets; the workflow writes the keystore to the runner's temporary folder and deletes it after the build. Without ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64, the release has no APK. Secret Value ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 The keystore, from base64 -w0 ~/uniform-chat-release.keystore ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS The alias, e.g. uniform-chat ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD The keystore password ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD The key password To build a signed APK locally, give the keystore and alias as properties and the passwords in the environment, never on the command line: read -rs ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD && export ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD="$ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD" dotnet publish src/Uniform.Chat.Android -c Release -p:Version=0.1.0 \ -p:AndroidSigningKeyStore=$HOME/uniform-chat-release.keystore -p:AndroidSigningKeyAlias=uniform-chat The version code follows the version: major × 10000 + minor × 100 + patch, so 0.2.1 is 201. It has to grow with every release that app stores get. Store listings fastlane/metadata/android/en-US/ holds the title, the short and full description, the icon, screenshots and a changelog per version code, e.g. changelogs/201.txt, in the layout F-Droid and IzzyOnDroid read. Add the changelog of a version before tagging it. Debian packages and the apt repository The workflow also packages the five Linux apps for Debian and Ubuntu, for amd64 and arm64, with packaging/linux/build-deb.sh. The packages are self-contained like the archives, and need only the system's usual libraries: Package Installs uniform-chat The desktop app in /opt/uniform-chat/desktop, the command uniform-chat, a menu entry and an icon uniform-chat-terminal The terminal client in /opt/uniform-chat/terminal, the command uniform-chat-terminal uniform-chat-server The server in /opt/uniform-chat/server, the command uniform-chat-server, and the system service uniform-chat-server run by the user uniform-chat, off until enabled; settings in /etc/uniform-chat-server, data in /var/lib/uniform-chat-server uniform-stun-server The STUN and TURN server in /opt/uniform-chat/stun, the command uniform-stun-server uniform-livekit-server The MatrixRTC authorization service in /opt/uniform-chat/livekit, the command uniform-livekit-server A prerelease's version gets a tilde, so that it sorts before its release: 0.2.0-rc.1 is 0.2.0~rc.1. The releases themselves are the apt repository, with no other hosting. Each release, but not a prerelease, gets an index as its assets, made by packaging/linux/build-apt-index.sh: Packages lists its own packages and, from the previous release's index, those of all earlier releases; Release has the hashes, InRelease and Release.gpg sign it, and uniform-chat-archive-keyring.gpg is the public key. apt reads it from https://github.com/tagcode/Uniform.Chat/releases/ with the suite latest/download/, which GitHub serves from the newest release, and fetches each package from download/<tag>/ there. So users can also install an earlier version, as long as its release exists. Prereleases have packages but are not in the index. Users add the repository once: sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/apt/keyrings curl -fsSL https://github.com/tagcode/Uniform.Chat/releases/latest/download/uniform-chat-archive-keyring.gpg | sudo tee /etc/apt/keyrings/uniform-chat.gpg > /dev/null echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/uniform-chat.gpg] https://github.com/tagcode/Uniform.Chat/releases/ latest/download/" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/uniform-chat.list sudo apt update The index is signed with a GPG key of its own. apt trusts packages by it, so keep it safe and backed up: with a new key, every user has to add the repository again. Create it once; gpg asks for a passphrase: gpg --quick-generate-key "Uniform Chat packages <tagcode@users.noreply.github.com>" rsa4096 sign never gpg --armor --export-secret-keys "Uniform Chat packages" > uniform-chat-apt-key.asc Then add these repository secrets, and keep uniform-chat-apt-key.asc with the other keys, not in the repository. Without APT_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY, releases have packages but no index. Secret Value APT_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY The contents of uniform-chat-apt-key.asc APT_GPG_PASSPHRASE Its passphrase To build a package locally, publish the app as the workflow does, then: packaging/linux/build-deb.sh server publish/uniform-chat-server-0.2.0-linux-x64 0.2.0 linux-x64 out Documentation on GitHub Pages After each release, but not a prerelease, the workflow publishes the documentation of that release on GitHub Pages, from the tagcode.github.io repository, in the same folders as here: Address Site https://tagcode.github.io/Uniform.Chat/docs/ This developer site, with the API reference https://tagcode.github.io/Uniform.Chat/user-docs/Uniform.Chat.Desktop/ The user guide of the desktop app; likewise Uniform.Chat.Android, Uniform.Chat.Terminal, Uniform.Chat.Server, Uniform.Stun.Server and Uniform.LiveKit.Server Each release replaces the previous documentation. The same job updates the F-Droid repository below, so both go into one commit. It needs the PAGES_TOKEN secret, described below; without the F-Droid secrets only the documentation is published. F-Droid repository After each release, but not a prerelease, the workflow adds the APK to the app's own F-Droid repository, which GitHub Pages serves from the tagcode.github.io repository at https://tagcode.github.io/fdroid/repo. fdroidserver reads the APKs, the store listing from fastlane/metadata/android/ and the app's entry from fdroid/metadata/rip.uniform.chat.yml, and signs the index with the repository key. The repository keeps only the newest version, as the site's space is limited; users can't go back to an older one through F-Droid. Prereleases are left out because they share the version code of their release. The repository key is separate from the app's release key. F-Droid users trust the repository by its fingerprint, so a lost key means they have to add the repository again. Create it once, outside the repository: keytool -genkeypair -keystore ~/uniform-chat-fdroid.keystore -alias fdroid-repo -keyalg RSA -keysize 4096 -sigalg SHA256withRSA -validity 10000 -dname "CN=Uniform Chat F-Droid repository" Then add these repository secrets. Without them, the release is not added to the F-Droid repository. Secret Value FDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 The keystore, from base64 -w0 ~/uniform-chat-fdroid.keystore FDROID_KEY_ALIAS The alias, e.g. fdroid-repo FDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD The keystore password, which the key shares PAGES_TOKEN A fine-grained token for tagcode/tagcode.github.io only, with Contents: Read and write Each update replaces the Pages repository's history with one commit, so the APKs of dropped versions and old documentation don't make it grow. The site's other files stay as they are. To be offered the repository, users open https://tagcode.github.io/fdroid/repo and scan or tap its link, which carries the key's fingerprint.

Uniform.Chat/documentation.html.title: Documentation | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/documentation.html.summary: Documentation DocFX is a local tool pinned in dotnet-tools.json. dotnet tool restore # Developer guide and API reference dotnet docfx docs/docfx.json # User guides: the desktop app, the Android app, the terminal client, the server dotnet docfx user-docs/Uniform.Chat.Desktop/docfx.json dotnet docfx user-docs/Uniform.Chat.Android/docfx.json dotnet docfx user-docs/Uniform.Chat.Terminal/docfx.json dotnet docfx user-docs/Uniform.Chat.Server/docfx.json --serve hosts the site at http://localhost:8080. Output goes to each site's _site/ folder, and generated API files go to docs/api/; both are ignored by git. Each app has its own guide in user-docs/, named after its project: Uniform.Chat.Desktop, Uniform.Chat.Android, Uniform.Chat.Terminal and Uniform.Chat.Server. The Android guide has its own start and getting-started pages and includes the rest from the desktop guide, as it is the same app. Text that more than one guide needs, such as how encryption, the recovery key and verification work, is written once in user-docs/Uniform.Matrix.Core and included with [!include[](../../Uniform.Matrix.Core/encryption.md)]; it is not a site of its own. dotnet tool restore # Developer guide and API reference dotnet docfx docs/docfx.json --serve # User guides: the desktop app, the Android app, the terminal client, the server dotnet docfx user-docs/Uniform.Chat.Desktop/docfx.json --serve dotnet docfx user-docs/Uniform.Chat.Android/docfx.json --serve dotnet docfx user-docs/Uniform.Chat.Terminal/docfx.json --serve dotnet docfx user-docs/Uniform.Chat.Server/docfx.json --serve All sites use DocFX's built-in statictoc template, which writes the table of contents into every page, so the guides also work opened from disk. theme/ holds only what differs from it, as each docfx.json layers it on top ("template": [ "statictoc", "../theme" ] here, "../../theme" in the user guides): the logo, logo_blue.svg (the source of the logo and app icons), the favicon, styles/main.css with the dark look, and styles/main.js with the table of contents highlighting. The top of main.css also keeps a few styles of the older DocFX version the theme was made with; when upgrading DocFX, rebuild and look at the sites, as files of the built-in template change under it. The release archives carry them that way: each archive has its own app's guide as a docs folder.

Uniform.Chat/index.html.title: Uniform.Matrix | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/index.html.summary: Uniform.Matrix Uniform Chat is a collection of applications for the Matrix chat protocol, and the Uniform.Matrix .NET 10 class libraries they are built on: the Uniform.Chat.* projects are the apps and the server program, the Uniform.Matrix.* projects the libraries, named after the protocol they implement.

Uniform.Chat/testing.html.title: Testing | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
Uniform.Chat/testing.html.summary: Testing The tests use xUnit v3 on Microsoft.Testing.Platform, enabled in global.json. The same file pins the .NET 10 SDK, its newest release, as a newer SDK on a build machine, such as .NET 11 on GitHub's runners, would otherwise run instead: .NET 11's dotnet test asks which device to run the Android app on, and stops. dotnet test # all tests dotnet test -- --filter-not-trait "Category=Live" # skip tests against the real server Unit tests replace the network with StubHandler, which records requests and returns canned responses. Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Crypto.Tests has round-trip and tamper tests of the managed Olm and Megolm (OlmTests), differential tests against native vodozemac (OracleTests: messages, out-of-order delivery, Megolm ratchet positions up to 2^32 − 1, backup encryption, SAS and pickles in both directions), and protocol tests where several OlmMachines talk through FakeKeyServer, an in-memory stand-in for the key, cross-signing, account data, backup and to-device endpoints. SecurityTests cover recovery on a new device, key forwarding between own devices and SAS verification there. Live tests (Category=Live) log in to a real homeserver with the accounts in testclient.txt at the repository root, which share one password: @localpart:server @localpart2:server @localpart3:server password: ... Both files are in .gitignore, as they hold a password and recovery keys; without testclient.txt the live tests are skipped. Uniform.Matrix.Server.Tests run the same encryption flows against the in-memory server, with no accounts needed. Most live tests use the first account. LiveSecurityTests use the second and third: the first run sets up cross-signing, key backup and a recovery key on them and saves the recovery keys in testclient-recovery.txt (user ID, tab, key); later runs recover with those keys. Every live test logs out at the end, so no stale devices are left on the account. Verification requests name the test device, so the account's other sessions are not asked. Uniform.Chat.Avalonia.Tests drive the app's view models against the in-memory server, with Avalonia's headless platform and Skia rendering, so they need no display. Set UNIFORM_MATRIX_SCREENSHOTS to a folder to save the rendered chat window there. They pin xUnit v3 3.2, as Avalonia.Headless.XUnit 12 does not run on xUnit 4. Native test oracle The client needs no native code. Tests can compare the managed encryption with native vodozemac, built from Rust into vodozemac_ffi: # Once: Rust in your home directory (pinned to 1.99.0 by native/vodozemac-ffi/rust-toolchain.toml) curl -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --no-modify-path --profile minimal --default-toolchain 1.99.0 # Build for this machine native/build.sh The library lands in tests/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Crypto.Tests/runtimes/<rid>/native/, which is not in git. Without it the differential tests in OracleTests are skipped. The server's own tests, with two servers federating in memory, are described in Uniform.Matrix.Server.

api/LiveKit.Proto.Sensitivity.html.summary: Enum Sensitivity Namespace: LiveKit.Proto Assembly: Uniform.LiveKit.Protocol.dll Syntax public enum Sensitivity Fields Name Description Unspecified Unannotated default — safe to log. Identifiers, IDs, timestamps, enums, status fields. Pii User-identifying or user-controlled data: display names, phone numbers, metadata, attributes, custom headers, auth usernames, semi-public account identifiers (AWS role ARNs, Azure account names). Recorded under a sensitivity tag by a sink that can tag; redacted by one that cannot. Secret Credentials and authentication material: passwords, access keys, session tokens, signing keys, API keys, ICE credentials. ALWAYS redacted: no sink may record it.

api/Uniform.Chat.Avalonia.ViewModels.htm.title: Namespace Uniform.Chat.Avalonia.ViewModels | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
api/Uniform.Chat.Avalonia.ViewModels.htm.summary: Namespace Uniform.Chat.Avalonia.ViewModels Classes ActionSheetViewModel The details and actions of a message or room, opened by a long press or a right click: on phones a sheet from the bottom, on desktops a menu whose details open the sheet. AdminAccountItem An account as the panel lists it. AdminReportItem A report as the panel lists it. AdminTokenItem A registration token as the panel lists it. AdminViewModel Server administration for server admins, over the server's admin API: users' reports, accounts with suspension, locks, passwords, admin rights, notices and deactivation, and registration tokens. AudioTestViewModel The audio test: plays the microphone back a second later, through Opus as in a call, to try the microphone and the speaker or earpiece. CallViewModel The call bar: the voice call that rings or runs, with answering, declining, hanging up, muting and the loudspeaker, and the caller's video when they send it; it tells about a call for a while after it ends. ChatViewModel The signed-in screen: the room list, the open room's messages and the message box. ConnectingViewModel Shown while the remembered account resumes its session. DeviceItem One of the user's devices (sessions). DirectoryViewModel The public room directory of the user's server or another one: search it and join a room. LicenseEntry A license text the app carries: its group, e.g. Packages, and name. LicensesViewModel The licenses of the app and of everything it bundles, as the licenses of the bundled libraries require it to show: the list, and the text of the chosen one. LogFileItem A session log in the list: its file and how it is named there. LoginViewModel The sign-in form: user ID, password, and the homeserver address for servers without discovery; it also creates accounts, with the registration token and the server's policies when the server asks for them. LogsViewModel The app's session logs, as the terminal client's log window shows them: the sessions, and the entries of the chosen one at a level and above, newest first, filtered by text. MainViewModel The app's current page: the sign-in form, resuming, or the chat screen; it owns the running connection. MemberItem A member of the open room, for its member list. MessageList The open room's timeline as items: events become messages, while edits, deletions and reactions change the messages they refer to. MessageViewModel One item of the open room's timeline. PublicRoomItem A room of a public room directory. RoomItemViewModel One room in the room list: name, latest message, unread count, and whether it is an invite, a direct chat or encrypted. SecurityViewModel Encryption status of this device and the account, with what is missing: set up recovery, recover with a key, or verify with another device; also the blocked users, and deleting the account. SettingsViewModel Appearance and notification settings, kept in the Ui section of the app's settings.json and saved on every change. SheetAction An action of an ActionSheetViewModel: it runs, or offers Choices such as report reasons. SheetDetail A line of an ActionSheetViewModel's details. StatusLine One labelled line of the security status. VerificationViewModel An emoji verification with another device as it goes: accept a request, compare emoji, then the outcome. VideoFeed The newest picture of a video, for a VideoView to show; pictures may come on any thread. ViewModelBase Base of the view models, with property change notification. Enums AdminSection A section of the server administration panel. AppTheme Colour theme of the app. MessageKind How a timeline item is shown.

api/Uniform.Chat.Avalonia.Views.html.title: Namespace Uniform.Chat.Avalonia.Views | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
api/Uniform.Chat.Avalonia.Views.html.summary: Namespace Uniform.Chat.Avalonia.Views Classes ActionSheetView The details and actions of a message or room, as a sheet: a title, details, quick reactions and a row per action. AdminView Server administration: reports, accounts and registration tokens. ChatView The chat screen: the room list and the open room; the code here handles scrolling, keys and the narrow layout. ConnectingView Progress while the remembered account resumes. DirectoryView The room directory: server and search fields, and the rooms found with a Join button each. LicensesView The licenses of the app and what it bundles: a list, and the chosen text. LinkClickedEventArgs Arguments of LinkClicked. LoginView The sign-in form, which also creates accounts. MainView Shows the current page of MainViewModel; on phones it makes room for the on-screen keyboard. MainWindow Desktop window around MainView; its title counts unread rooms, and its focus decides whether notifications show. RichText Message text that shows the HTML formatted_body of Matrix messages as styled, selectable text: emphasis, code, quotes, lists, headings, links and mentions. SecurityView Encryption status with recovery set-up, recovery and verification. SenderColorConverter Turn a user or room ID into one of a few colours, the same one every time, for names and avatars. SettingsView Appearance and notification settings, and the logs, licences and audio test in their place. TextScale Text sizes of the app scaled from the chosen base size: the titles, small and tiny texts of Styles.axaml grow and shrink with it. VerificationView An emoji verification with another device. VideoView Shows the newest picture of a VideoFeed, turned upright by its rotation and scaled to fit with its aspect ratio kept; a new picture is drawn at most once per rendered frame, and pictures that come meanwhile are skipped.

api/Uniform.Chat.Server.Ui.html.title: Namespace Uniform.Chat.Server.Ui | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
api/Uniform.Chat.Server.Ui.html.summary: Namespace Uniform.Chat.Server.Ui Classes AdminWindow<T> Base of the admin lists: a header, a list of rows, details of the selected row, and action buttons. DashboardOptions What a dashboard may do besides the admin lists, which depends on how it reaches the server. ReportsWindow Users' reports of events, rooms and users, newest first; reports can be resolved, opened again or deleted, and resolved ones shown or hidden. RoomsWindow Rooms of the server, with their members and directory listing; rooms can be listed or unlisted in the public room directory. ServerWindow Server dashboard: identity, addresses and live counters, the user, room and report windows, and the shared settings and log windows where the server's files can be reached. It runs in the server's own process, or in a manager attached to a running server. UsersWindow Accounts of the server: create users, reset passwords, give admin rights, suspend, lock, deactivate.

api/Uniform.LiveKit.html.summary: Namespace Uniform.LiveKit Classes FrameCryptor LiveKit's end-to-end encryption of media frames, as its clients and Element Call do it: AES-GCM with a key derived by HKDF, the first bytes of each frame in the clear and authenticated, and the IV and the key's index after the frame. LiveKitMedia The media of a call through LiveKit, as one IMediaConnection: this side's frames encrypted and sent on the room it publishes to, and the others' received on the rooms it subscribes to, decrypted with each sender's key. LiveKitRoom A participant's connection to a LiveKit room: the signalling, the subscriber peer connection the server offers with the others' tracks, and the publisher peer connection this side offers with its own. LiveKitRoomOptions Options of a LiveKitRoom. LiveKitRoomService Calls LiveKit's room service over Twirp with JSON, authorized by a short access token signed with the API secret. LiveKitSignalClient LiveKit's signalling: a WebSocket to the server's /rtc, with protobuf SignalRequest messages out and SignalResponse messages in, and the pings that keep it open. MatrixRtcAuthorizationClient Asks a MatrixRTC authorization service, e.g. lk-jwt-service from a homeserver's rtc_foci, for LiveKit's URL and a token to join a call with. Enums FrameKind The kind of a frame, which decides how many of its first bytes stay unencrypted, so that an SFU and the packetizer still read them.

api/Uniform.Matrix.Calls.VideoReceiver.h.title: Class VideoReceiver | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
api/Uniform.Matrix.Calls.VideoReceiver.h.summary: Class VideoReceiver Decodes the video a peer connection receives, on its own task, and gives the pictures in PictureDecoded. Inheritance object VideoReceiver Implements IAsyncDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Namespace: Uniform.Matrix.Calls Assembly: Uniform.Matrix.Calls.dll Syntax public sealed class VideoReceiver : IAsyncDisposable Remarks A platform decoder that gives too few pictures at first is replaced by the C# one. A device that cannot keep up, by its decode times or by falling behind, asks the sender for less with a REMB, and for full quality again once it has room. Frames queue as they arrive. When decoding falls behind by Uniform.Matrix.Calls.VideoReceiver.MaxQueued frames, or a frame does not decode, the frames up to the next keyframe are skipped and the peer is asked for one, as inter frames only decode after the frames before them. api/Uniform.Matrix.Calls.html.title: Namespace Uniform.Matrix.Calls | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
api/Uniform.Matrix.Calls.html.summary: Namespace Uniform.Matrix.Calls Classes CallService Matrix 1:1 calls of the logged-in user: places calls, raises incoming ones, and routes the events of the synced timelines to their VoiceCall; sends through the outbox, which encrypts in encrypted rooms. LegacyCall One Matrix 1:1 call of m.call.* events, version 1, as Element Web and SchildiChat Legacy call: the invite, answer and select_answer, trickled candidates, and the hangup or reject; with the media of an AudioPeerConnection and VoiceMedia, and the video a caller sends through VideoReceiver. RtcCall A 1:1 call over MatrixRTC, as Element X and Element Call make them: each side's membership in the room's call as a state event, a ring notification, the media through LiveKit SFUs, and the frames encrypted with keys sent to each member's device. VideoReceiver Decodes the video a peer connection receives, on its own task, and gives the pictures in PictureDecoded. VoiceCall A 1:1 call with another user, as the apps show it: its state, mute and camera, and the other's pictures; a LegacyCall of m.call.* events, or a RtcCall of MatrixRTC through a LiveKit SFU. VoiceMedia The voice of a call: the microphone's frames encoded with Opus and sent over a peer connection, and the frames received put in order by a jitter buffer, decoded, and played as the speaker needs them. Interfaces IVideoCamera A camera with its VP8 encoder, as a platform gives it for a call's video, e.g. Android's camera and hardware encoder; started when the call connects, disposed when it ends. Enums CallState The state of a VoiceCall. Delegates CallEventSender Sends a call event into the call's room.

api/Uniform.Matrix.Client.Services.html.title: Namespace Uniform.Matrix.Client.Services | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
api/Uniform.Matrix.Client.Services.html.summary: Namespace Uniform.Matrix.Client.Services Classes AccountRegistration Create an account before the first sign-in: find the server, learn what registering needs there, and register without logging in, so the apps then sign in the usual way. ClientSession Owns the MatrixClient: resumes the stored session or logs in, and stores new sessions. ConnectionStatus Current connection state, published by MatrixWorker; Changed fires on the worker's thread. CryptoService End-to-end encryption of the client: owns the OlmMachine, decrypts syncs and encrypts outgoing events. EncryptionUnavailableException A message for an encrypted room cannot be encrypted, so it is not sent. MatrixWorker Background service that prepares the database, connects, then runs sync and the outbox until shutdown. MediaCache Downloads media and thumbnails once and serves them from the account's media directory afterwards. NetworkMonitor Tells when the device's network changed, e.g. another Wi-Fi or mobile data, so that the sync and calls can move to it at once instead of waiting for requests on the old network to time out. OutboxSender Sends queued messages in order, keeping them in the database until the server accepts them. SyncProcessor Applies sync responses to the in-memory RoomStore and the database, and publishes the changes to the frontend. Interfaces ICredentialPrompt Asks the user for a password; implemented by the active frontend. Enums ConnectionState Connection state shown by the UI.

api/Uniform.Matrix.Client.Storage.html.summary: Namespace Uniform.Matrix.Client.Storage Classes ClientDbContext EF Core context of the local SQLite database. StoredEvent Room event received from the server. StoredMedia Downloaded media file kept in the media directory. Enums OutboxState Delivery state of an OutboxMessage.

MatrixClient.Sync.cs: sync, sync loop and filters. MatrixClient.Rooms.cs: room membership, creation, aliases, state and members. MatrixClient.Events.cs: room history, sending, redaction, typing and read markers. MatrixClient.Profile.cs: profiles and presence. MatrixClient.AccountData.cs: account data, tags, ignored users and direct rooms. MatrixClient.PushRules.cs: push rules and pushers. api/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Core.html.title: Namespace Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Core | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
api/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Core.html.summary: Namespace Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Core Classes AdminAccount A local account in Synapse's user admin API. AdminAccountsResponse A page of AdminAccounts. AdminRegistrationToken A registration token in Synapse's admin API. AdminRegistrationTokensResponse Response listing AdminRegistrationTokens. AdminReport A report in Synapse's event report admin API; this project's server lists reports of rooms and users there too. AdminReportsResponse A page of AdminReports. AdminRoomInfo A room in Synapse's room admin API. AdminRoomShutdown Response of shutting down a room. AdminRoomsResponse A page of AdminRoomInfos. AuthFlow One accepted combination of auth stages. AuthTypes Common authentication types. Base64 Base64 forms used by Matrix: unpadded for keys and ciphertexts, padded by some clients, URL-safe in JWKs; decoding accepts all. CallAnswerContent Content of CallAnswer. CallCandidate An ICE candidate of CallCandidatesContent; an empty Candidate ends the candidates. CallCandidatesContent Content of CallCandidates. CallContent Fields every call event has. CallEncryptionKeysContent Content of CallEncryptionKeys, sent to each member's device over Olm: the sender's key that its media is encrypted with. CallHangupContent Content of CallHangup. CallInviteContent Content of CallInvite. CallKeyMember The sender of CallEncryptionKeysContent. CallMediaKey A media key of a call member, in CallEncryptionKeysContent. CallMemberContent Content of CallMember, a device's membership in a room's call, as Element Call writes it; empty when the device left. CallNegotiateContent Content of CallNegotiate: a new offer or its answer during a call, e.g. to restart ICE after a network change. CallRejectContent Content of CallReject. CallSelectAnswerContent Content of CallSelectAnswer. CallSessionDescription An SDP offer or answer. CanonicalAliasContent Content of m.room.canonical_alias. CanonicalJson Canonical JSON: keys sorted by code point, no whitespace, minimal escaping; the form that Matrix signatures are made over. ClientEvent Room event as returned by sync, messages and state endpoints, see room event format. ContextResponse Response of GET /_matrix/client/v3/rooms/{roomId}/context/{eventId}. CreateContent Content of m.room.create. CreateMediaResponse Response of creating media before uploading its content. CreateRoomRequest Request of POST /_matrix/client/v3/createRoom. CrossSigningKey A cross-signing key: master, self-signing or user-signing. CrossSigningUsages Usages of Usage. DelayedEventResponse Response of sending a delayed event. Device A device, i.e. one logged-in session, of the user. DeviceKeys Signed device keys as uploaded and queried. DeviceLists Device list changes of a SyncResponse. DevicesResponse Response of GET /_matrix/client/v3/devices. DirectContent Content of m.direct: user ID to direct-message room IDs. EncryptedContent Content of m.room.encrypted, both Olm and Megolm. EncryptedFile Encrypted attachment: where the ciphertext is and how to decrypt it. EncryptionAlgorithms Encryption algorithm names. EncryptionContent Content of m.room.encryption. ErrorCodes Common error codes. ErrorResponse Standard error body returned with non-2xx responses. EventFilter Filter for non-room events. EventIdResponse Response holding an event ID, e.g. of send and redact. EventList<T> List of events. EventTypes Well-known event types. ExceptionText Text of exceptions for logs and messages. Filter Sync filter; upload with MatrixClient.CreateFilterAsync or pass ToJson() inline. FilterIdResponse Response of POST /_matrix/client/v3/user/{userId}/filter. FullyReadContent Content of m.fully_read. IgnoredUserListContent Content of m.ignored_user_list. InReplyTo Reply target of InReplyTo. InitialStateEvent State event of InitialState. InvitedRoom Update of an invited room. JoinedMembersResponse Response of GET /_matrix/client/v3/rooms/{roomId}/joined_members. JoinedRoom Update of a joined room. JoinedRoomsResponse Response of GET /_matrix/client/v3/joined_rooms. JsonWebKey JSON Web Key of an EncryptedFile. KeyBackupAlgorithms Algorithms of Algorithm. KeyBackupData One backed-up session key. KeyBackupVersion Key backup version from GET /room_keys/version. KeysBackup Backed-up keys by room ID, as uploaded and downloaded by /room_keys/keys. KeysClaimResponse Response of POST /_matrix/client/v3/keys/claim. KeysQueryResponse Response of POST /_matrix/client/v3/keys/query. KeysUploadResponse Response of POST /_matrix/client/v3/keys/upload. KnockedRoom Update of a room the user knocked on. LeftRoom Update of a left room. LoginFlow One supported login type, e.g. m.login.password. LoginFlowsResponse Response of GET /_matrix/client/v3/login. LoginResponse Response of POST /_matrix/client/v3/login. MatrixEvent Event with a type and content; used as is for account data and ephemeral events. MatrixException A homeserver returned a Matrix error, e.g. M_FORBIDDEN or M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN. MatrixJson Shared JSON settings matching Matrix wire conventions. MatrixLink Link to a room, a user or an event: a matrix.to link, a matrix: URI or a bare identifier. MediaInfo Attachment metadata of Info, see m.file. MemberContent Content of m.room.member; state key is the user ID. MembersResponse Response of GET /_matrix/client/v3/rooms/{roomId}/members. Memberships Membership states of Membership. Mentions Intentional mentions of a message. MessageContent Content of m.room.message. MessageFormats Formats of Format. MessageTypes Message types of MessageType. MessagesResponse Response of GET /_matrix/client/v3/rooms/{roomId}/messages. NameContent Content of m.room.name. OpenIdTokenResponse Response of POST /user/{userId}/openid/request_token: a token that proves the user to another service. PasswordLoginRequest Request of POST /_matrix/client/v3/login with type m.login.password. PowerLevelsContent Content of m.room.power_levels: who may do what in a room, as levels from 0 up, where 100 is usually an admin and 50 a moderator. PresenceContent Content of m.presence, also the presence status response. PresenceEvent Presence update of Sender, content PresenceContent. PresenceStates Presence states. ProfileResponse Response of GET /_matrix/client/v3/profile/{userId}. PublicRoom Room listed in the public room directory. PublicRoomsResponse Response of GET /_matrix/client/v3/publicRooms. ReactionContent Content of m.reaction. ReceiptContent Content of m.receipt: event ID, then receipt type, then user ID. ReceiptInfo One receipt of ReceiptContent. ReceiptTypes Receipt types. RedactionContent Content of m.room.redaction. RegisterRequest Request of POST /_matrix/client/v3/register. RegisterResponse Response of POST /_matrix/client/v3/register; tokens are missing when login was inhibited. Relation Relation between events. RelationTypes Relation types of RelType. RoomAliasResponse Response of GET /_matrix/client/v3/directory/room/{roomAlias}. RoomAliasesResponse Response of GET /_matrix/client/v3/rooms/{roomId}/aliases. RoomAvatarContent Content of m.room.avatar. RoomEventFilter Filter for room events. RoomFilter Filter for room data. RoomIdResponse Response holding a room ID, e.g. of join and create room. RoomKeyBackup Backed-up keys of one room, by session ID. RoomKeyContent Content of m.room_key, received over Olm. RoomMember Joined member of JoinedMembersResponse. RoomPresets Presets of Preset. RoomSummary Room summary for computing a room name. RoomTags Predefined room tags. RtcDeclineContent Content of RtcDecline: the callee declined the call of a notification. RtcFocusActive The focus a member uses, in FocusActive: LiveKit, each member on the SFU of its own homeserver. RtcNotificationContent Content of RtcNotification: a call started, ringing the others' devices for Lifetime. RtcTransport A MatrixRTC transport: how media goes, e.g. a LiveKit SFU behind its authorization service. RtcTransportsResponse Response of GET /_matrix/client/unstable/org.matrix.msc4143/rtc/transports: the homeserver's transports, preferred first. StringOrNumberConverter Reads a JSON string or number as text, as call versions are either; writes text. StrippedStateEvent Partial state of an invited room, see stripped state. SyncResponse Response of GET /_matrix/client/v3/sync. SyncRooms Room updates of a SyncResponse by membership, keyed by room ID. TagContent Content of m.tag, also the tags response. TagInfo One tag of TagContent. TermsPolicy A policy of the Terms stage, such as terms of service, that the user reads and accepts, in one language. Timeline Timeline section of a room update. ToDeviceEvent Send-to-device event of ToDevice. TopicContent Content of m.room.topic. TurnServerResponse Response of GET /_matrix/client/v3/voip/turnServer: time-limited TURN credentials; empty when the server has no TURN. TypingContent Content of m.typing. UnreadNotificationCounts Unread notification counts of a room. UnsignedData Server-added unsigned data of a ClientEvent. UploadResponse Response of POST /_matrix/media/v3/upload. UserDirectoryEntry User found by MatrixClient.SearchUsersAsync. UserDirectoryResponse Response of POST /_matrix/client/v3/user_directory/search. UserIdentifier Identifier of type m.id.user. UserInteractiveAuthResponse 401 body of the user-interactive auth API. VerificationRequestContent Content of an in-room verification request: an m.room.message of msgtype m.key.verification.request. VersionsResponse Response of GET /_matrix/client/versions. WellKnownClient Body of GET /.well-known/matrix/client. WellKnownServer The m.homeserver entry of WellKnownClient. WhoAmIResponse Response of GET /_matrix/client/v3/account/whoami. WhoisConnection A connection of a WhoisSession. WhoisDevice A device in a WhoisResponse. WhoisResponse Response of whois: a user's devices and their connections. WhoisSession A session of a WhoisDevice. Structs MxcUri Content URI of the form mxc://server/mediaId. UserId User ID of the form @localpart:server. Enums Direction Pagination direction of MatrixClient.GetMessagesAsync.

api/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Crypto.OlmMa.title: Class OlmMachine | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
api/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Crypto.OlmMa.summary: Class OlmMachine End-to-end encryption state machine of one device: keys, Olm sessions with other devices and Megolm sessions for rooms. Inheritance object OlmMachine Implements IDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Namespace: Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Crypto Assembly: Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Crypto.dll Syntax public sealed class OlmMachine : IDisposable Remarks Feed every sync to ReceiveSyncAsync(SyncResponse, CancellationToken), decrypt m.room.encrypted timeline events with DecryptRoomEventAsync(string, ClientEvent, CancellationToken), and encrypt outgoing events for encrypted rooms with EncryptRoomEventAsync(string, string, object, IReadOnlyCollection<string>, EncryptionContent?, CancellationToken). Calls are serialized, so it can be shared between threads. Split into partial files: OlmMachine.cs: account, key upload and device lists. OlmMachine.Olm.cs: Olm sessions and to-device messages, including received room keys. OlmMachine.Megolm.cs: room message encryption, key sharing and decryption. OlmMachine.CrossSigning.cs: cross-signing keys, trust and recovery from secret storage. OlmMachine.Backup.cs: server-side key backup. OlmMachine.KeyRequests.cs: room key and secret requests between the user's own devices. OlmMachine.Verification.cs: SAS emoji verification of devices. Examples OlmMachine machine = await OlmMachine.CreateAsync(new MatrixKeyTransport(client), store, client.UserId!, client.DeviceId!, pickleKey); await foreach (SyncResponse sync in client.SyncLoopAsync()) { await machine.ReceiveSyncAsync(sync); // decrypt timeline events with machine.DecryptRoomEventAsync(roomId, ev) } Fields | Edit this page View Source WedgedSessionRetry How long before a device whose message could not be decrypted gets another new session. api/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Crypto.html.title: Namespace Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Crypto | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
api/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Crypto.html.summary: Namespace Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Crypto Classes AccountRecord Stored Olm account. AesCtr AES-256 in counter mode with a 128-bit big-endian counter, built from ECB as .NET has no CTR mode. AttachmentCrypto Encryption of attachments in encrypted rooms: AES-256-CTR, then SHA-256 of the ciphertext. AttachmentKeys Key and hash of an encrypted attachment, the file object of a message without its URL. DecryptedToDeviceEvent A to-device event decrypted from Olm, with the keys of the device that sent it. DeviceInfo A device of a user, from verified device keys. DeviceListRecord Stored device list of a user. Ed25519 Standalone Ed25519 keys, e.g. for cross-signing; keys and signatures are unpadded base64. EncryptedAttachments Message content of encrypted attachments; upload and download are in Uniform.Matrix.Client. EncryptedSecret Secret as stored in secret storage account data: iv, ciphertext and mac. EstablishedSas Shared secret of a SAS verification: emoji or decimals to compare, and MACs over the keys being verified. IdentityKeys Public identity keys of an account, unpadded base64. InMemoryCryptoStore ICryptoStore in memory, for tests and short-lived clients. InboundGroupSessionRecord Stored Megolm session for decrypting one sender's room messages. MegolmInboundSession Inbound Megolm session: decrypts one sender's room messages from the index its key was shared at. api/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Server.html.title: Namespace Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Server | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
api/Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Server.html.summary: Namespace Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Server Classes AuthEventTypes Event types that take part in authorization. AuthEvents The auth events selection: which state an event's authorization depends on. AuthRules The authorization rules of room versions 10, 11 and 12: whether an event is allowed given the state it depends on. DnsSrv DNS messages for SRV lookups, as RFC 1035 lays them out: a query for one name, and the SRV records of its answer. EventFormat Hashing, IDs, signatures and redaction of persistent data units, the events of the room graph. FederationAuth Request authentication between servers: the sender signs the method, URI, both server names and the JSON body, and puts the signature in an X-Matrix Authorization header. PowerLevels A room's power levels with the spec's defaults filled in. PushContext Facts about the room and the user that push rule conditions need, besides the event itself. PushDecision What the push rules say about one event for one user: whether it counts as a notification, and whether it is highlighted, e.g. as a mention. PushRules Push rules: the server-default rule set and the evaluation of a rule set against an event. RoomVersion A room version: the rules of event format, redaction and authorization a room follows. ServerAcl A room's server access control list, m.room.server_acl: which servers may take part in the room. ServerNames Server names: a DNS name, IPv4 address or bracketed IPv6 address, with an optional port. SrvRecord A DNS SRV record: where a service of a domain runs. StateResolution State resolution v2, and its v2.1 form in room version 12: the room's state where the room's history has forks, from the states of each branch. XMatrixAuthorization The X-Matrix Authorization header parameters of a server-to-server request. Enums RedactionRules Redaction algorithm of a room version.

api/Uniform.Matrix.Server.Accounts.html.title: Namespace Uniform.Matrix.Server.Accounts | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
api/Uniform.Matrix.Server.Accounts.html.summary: Namespace Uniform.Matrix.Server.Accounts Classes AccountDataService A user's account data, global and per room, including room tags. AccountDeactivation Deactivates an account at its owner's request: leaves its rooms, clears its profile and ends its sessions; the user ID is never given out again. AccountService Local accounts, devices and access tokens. AdminDevice A device of a user, as whois shows it. AdminRoom A room as the admin screens list it. AdminService Server administration: accounts, passwords, admin rights and the room directory for the dashboard, and the same with suspension, locks, rooms and media for the remote admin API. AdminUser A local account as the admin screens list it. AdminUserChange What the remote admin API changes of an account; a null field stays as it is. AuthenticationRequiredException A request needs more user-interactive auth; answered with 401 and Response. LocalUserIds Rules for user IDs of local accounts. OpenIdTokens OpenID tokens: short-lived tokens a user hands to a service, which asks this server who they belong to through /_matrix/federation/v1/openid/userinfo. PresenceService Presence, kept in memory: what users set, and online while they sync. ProfileService Profiles: display name and avatar of local users, and of other servers' users through federation. PushNotifier Sends push notifications: follows the ServerStream, runs the push rules of the room's members on each new event, and posts to the push gateways of their http pushers. PushRuleService A user's push rules, kept as the m.push_rules account data that clients sync, and the unread counts they give. PusherService Users' pushers: where push notifications go, set by apps that want them, such as phone apps with a push gateway. RegistrationToken A registration token as the admin API shows it. RegistrationTokens Registration tokens: those in RegistrationTokens, which never run out, and those admins create in the database, with a number of uses and an expiry. Requester The authenticated user and device of a request. RoomShutdown What shutting down a room did. ServerNotices Server notices: messages from the server to a local user, in a room of their own tagged m.server_notice, where only the notices account may write. UserInteractiveAuth Runs user-interactive auth: sessions of completed stages, kept in memory for a short while. Structs Optional<T> A value that may be left out, as opposed to given as null.

api/Uniform.Matrix.Server.Federation.htm.title: Namespace Uniform.Matrix.Server.Federation | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
api/Uniform.Matrix.Server.Federation.htm.summary: Namespace Uniform.Matrix.Server.Federation Classes FederationClient Requests to other servers, signed with this server's key as FederationAuth describes. FederationEndpoint Endpoint metadata of federation endpoints: they answer only with federation on, and when Signed, only requests signed by the server they come from. FederationQueue Outgoing transactions, one queue per destination server: PDUs and EDUs are batched, and retried with growing pauses while the server cannot be reached. FederationSender Sends new room events to the other servers in each room as transactions: events of local users, and joins of remote users that this server accepted as the room's server; and device changes and presence of local users as m.device_list_update and m.presence EDUs. RemoteActivity Typing, read receipts and received presence with other servers: local users' ones go to the room's other servers as EDUs, and theirs are shown here. RemoteDevices End-to-end encryption with other servers' users: their device and one-time keys from their servers, and to-device messages to them, such as room keys, as m.direct_to_device EDUs. RemoteEvents Events other servers send in transactions: their senders' keys are gathered, and when they build on events this server does not have, those are asked for with get_missing_events and accepted first. RemoteInvites Invites of other servers' users: the invite is signed here, sent to the invitee's server, which signs it too, and then stored like any event. RemoteJoins Joining rooms of other servers: make_join for a template, sign it, send_join, check the returned state and store the room. RemoteServerKeys Other servers' signing keys: fetched from each server's /_matrix/key/v2/server, else from the TrustedKeyServers, and kept in the database until their valid_until_ts, at most a week. RoomAcls The server ACLs of rooms here: requests and transactions of a server the room's m.room.server_acl denies are refused for that room. RoomHistory Room history for other servers, which fill gaps with it before they can show new events: missing events, backfill, single events and the state at an event. ServerAddress Where to reach a server: the base address, whose host the TLS certificate must be valid for, and the Host header. ServerAuthentication Checks signed requests of other servers on endpoints with FederationEndpoint metadata, and tells endpoints who sent them, see GetOrigin(HttpContext). ServerResolver Resolve server names to addresses: IP literals and names with a port directly, otherwise through /.well-known/matrix/server delegation, then SRV records (_matrix-fed._tcp, and the older _matrix._tcp), else port 8448. SrvLookup Looks up DNS SRV records over UDP at the system's name servers, for resolving server names that delegate with _matrix-fed._tcp.

api/Uniform.Matrix.Server.Storage.html.title: Namespace Uniform.Matrix.Server.Storage | Uniform Chat Developer Guide
api/Uniform.Matrix.Server.Storage.html.summary: Namespace Uniform.Matrix.Server.Storage Classes AccessTokenRow An access token, stored as its SHA-256 hash so a leaked database does not leak sessions. AccountDataRow Account data of a user: global when RoomId is empty, else for one room. CounterRow A named counter of the server, such as the last ServerStream position. CrossSigningKeyRow A cross-signing key of a user. CurrentStateRow The current state of a room, one row per type and state key, for fast reads. DataDirectoryInUseException Another server process uses the data directory; stop it first. DataDirectoryLock Keeps other server processes off a data directory while this one uses it: LockFileName is held open exclusively, which on Linux is an flock that the kernel releases when the process ends, also when it is killed, so the lock never goes stale. DatabaseMigrator Creates or upgrades the schema at start, before the server accepts requests, in write-ahead log mode so reads do not block writes; and flushes the database at stop. DelayedEventRow A delayed event (MSC4140) waiting to be sent, kept so that a restart of the server does not forget it. DesignTimeServerDbContextFactory Context for dotnet ef at design time, on a throwaway SQLite file. DeviceKeysRow The signed device keys of a device, without signatures others uploaded later. DeviceListChangeRow The latest change of a user's devices or cross-signing keys, which others' syncs report in device_lists.changed. DeviceRow A device of a local user. EventEdgeRow Edge of the room graph: an event and one of its previous events. EventRelationRow A relation of an event to another, from its m.relates_to, for threads and relation lookups. EventRow An event of the room graph, stored as its PDU JSON without the event ID. FallbackKeyRow The fallback key of a device for one algorithm, given out when its one-time keys run out. FederationOutboxRow A PDU or EDU waiting to be sent to another server, kept so a restart does not lose it; deleted once sent or refused for good. FederationProgressRow How far the federation sender has handed the stream to its queue, so a restart continues there and misses nothing; one row. FilterRow A stored sync filter of a user. ForgottenRoomRow A room a user has forgotten, so it no longer shows in their sync. ForwardExtremityRow A forward extremity: an event of the room that no other event follows yet; new events point at these. KeyBackupVersionRow A key backup version of a user. KeySignatureRow A signature uploaded later for a device key or a master key, kept apart so each user sees only the signatures meant for them. MediaRow A file in the media repository, uploaded by a local user; the bytes are stored in the media directory. OneTimeKeyRow An unclaimed one-time key of a device. ProfileRow A user's profile. PusherRow A pusher: where to send push notifications of a user, usually a push gateway that wakes a phone app. ReceiptRow A user's latest receipt of one type and thread in a room. RegistrationTokenRow A registration token an admin created, as Synapse's admin API manages them. RemoteInviteRow An invite from another server to a room not on this server yet, with the room's stripped state; joining the room or rejecting the invite ends it. RemoteMediaRow Media of another server, fetched once and kept here; its file and thumbnails are stored under LocalId, an ID of this server, as other servers' IDs are not safe as paths. ReportRow A user's report of an event, room or user, for the admin to review. RoomAliasRow A local room alias. RoomKeyRow A backed-up room key of one session. RoomRow A room known to the server. ServerDbContext The homeserver's database; SQLite now, PostgreSQL later through the same model. ServerKeyResponseRow Another server's signed key answer, as /_matrix/key/v2/server gave it, kept so a restart or a server that is down does not stop checking its signatures; the latest per server. StateGroupEntryRow One state entry of a state group. StateGroupRow A room state snapshot, stored as changes against a parent group. ThumbnailRow A generated thumbnail of a MediaRow, stored next to it. ToDeviceRow A to-device message waiting for its device's next sync. TransactionRow A client transaction ID mapped to the event it created, so retried sends are not duplicated. UserRow A local user account.

api/Uniform.Matrix.WebRtc.AudioPeerConne.summary: Class AudioPeerConnection A WebRTC peer connection with one Opus audio stream each way, as 1:1 voice calls use: SDP offer and answer, ICE with trickled candidates, DTLS-SRTP, and RTP; and, when the peer offers it and ReceiveVideo is set, VP8 video received. The caller calls CreateOffer(bool) and later AcceptAnswer(string); the callee calls AcceptOffer(string). Both trickle the candidates of CandidateGathered to the peer, give the peer's to AddRemoteCandidate(string), and call ConnectAsync(CancellationToken). api/Uniform.Matrix.WebRtc.Ice.IceAgent.h.summary: Class IceAgent A full ICE agent for one component over UDP, IPv4 and IPv6, as WebRTC's bundled, RTCP-multiplexed media needs: gathers candidates, checks pairs with the peer, selects one, and carries datagrams over it. Inheritance object IceAgent Implements IAsyncDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Namespace: Uniform.Matrix.WebRtc.Ice Assembly: Uniform.Matrix.WebRtc.dll Syntax public sealed class IceAgent : IAsyncDisposable Remarks One IPv4 socket bound to all interfaces is the base of every IPv4 host candidate, and of the server-reflexive ones; each TURN allocation on that socket is the base of a relayed candidate. An IPv6 socket is likewise the base of the IPv6 host candidates, which are preferred, as RFC 8421 recommends. So pairs are bases times remote candidates of the same family; relays, being IPv4, pair with IPv4 peers. Candidates trickle: CandidateGathered raises each as found, and AddRemoteCandidate(IceCandidate) takes the peer's at any time. The controlling agent nominates the best pair that works, shortly after the first one does; checks then continue every few seconds, for consent. Datagrams that are not STUN, i.e. DTLS and SRTP, go to DataReceived. Constructors | Edit this page View Source IceAgent(IceOptions) Open the socket, and start reading it. api/Uniform.Matrix.WebRtc.Rtp.Vp8Depacke.summary: Class Vp8Depacketizer Puts VP8 frames together from RTP packets, RFC 7741: the packets of a frame share a timestamp, the first starts partition 0, and the last has the marker bit. Packets may come out of order; frames are given in order. Inheritance object Vp8Depacketizer Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Namespace: Uniform.Matrix.WebRtc.Rtp Assembly: Uniform.Matrix.WebRtc.dll Syntax public sealed class Vp8Depacketizer Remarks A frame waits while packets before it may still come, until the newest packet is a reorder window past the gap: then they count as lost. While a keyframe is needed, a complete one does not wait, as it decodes on its own. A frame after lost packets cannot be decoded, as it predicts from the frames before; from then on only a keyframe is given, and NeedsKeyframe tells the caller to ask the sender for one, e.g. with an RTCP PLI. Puts VP8 frames together from RTP packets, RFC 7741: the packets of a frame share a timestamp, the first starts partition 0, and the last has the marker bit. Packets may come out of order; frames are given in order. Declaration public Vp8Depacketizer(int reorderWindow = 64, byte? orientationId = null) Parameters Type Name Description int reorderWindow How many packets past a gap may arrive before the missing ones count as lost. byte? orientationId The header extension ID of the video orientation, whose rotation the frames carry from their last packet; null when not used. Remarks A frame waits while packets before it may still come, until the newest packet is a reorder window past the gap: then they count as lost. While a keyframe is needed, a complete one does not wait, as it decodes on its own. A frame after lost packets cannot be decoded, as it predicts from the frames before; from then on only a keyframe is given, and NeedsKeyframe tells the caller to ask the sender for one, e.g. with an RTCP PLI. api/Uniform.Matrix.WebRtc.Srtp.SrtpSessi.summary: Class SrtpSession One direction of SRTP and SRTCP with the AES_CM_128_HMAC_SHA1_80 suite, which WebRTC requires: protects outgoing packets, or checks and decrypts incoming ones. Inheritance object SrtpSession Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Namespace: Uniform.Matrix.WebRtc.Srtp Assembly: Uniform.Matrix.WebRtc.dll Syntax public sealed class SrtpSession Remarks Keys come from a master key and salt, as DTLS-SRTP exports them, with the key derivation rate 0. Each SSRC keeps its own rollover counter, which extends the 16-bit sequence number to the 48-bit packet index, and a 64-packet replay window. An SRTP packet is the RTP header, the payload encrypted with AES in counter mode, and an 80-bit HMAC-SHA1 tag over the header, the encrypted payload and the rollover counter. SRTCP also encrypts all after the first eight bytes, and appends the E flag and a 31-bit index before its tag. api/Uniform.Stun.Protocol.html.summary: Namespace Uniform.Stun.Protocol Classes ChannelData TURN channel data: a channel number, a length, and the data, with four bytes of overhead instead of a Send or Data indication's thirty-six. StunAddress The address attributes of STUN: XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS and the like, whose port and address are XOR'ed with the magic cookie and, for IPv6, the transaction ID, so that middleboxes do not rewrite them. StunMessage A STUN message: method, class, transaction ID and attributes, parsed from or encoded to the wire with optional MESSAGE-INTEGRITY and FINGERPRINT. TurnCredentials Time-limited TURN credentials from a secret shared by a TURN server and the service that hands them out, such as a Matrix homeserver's /voip/turnServer: the user name is expiry:name, with the expiry in Unix seconds, and the password is the Base64 HMAC-SHA1 of the user name with the secret. api/Uniform.Stun.TurnClient.html.summary: Class TurnClient A TURN client over UDP: allocates a relayed address on a TURN server, permits peers, and relays datagrams to and from them, refreshing all until closed. api/Uniform.Turn.TurnServer.html.summary: Class TurnServer A STUN and TURN server: answers Binding requests, and relays UDP between authenticated clients and their peers. Clients reach it over UDP, TCP or TLS; peers over UDP. Inheritance object TurnServer Implements IAsyncDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Namespace: Uniform.Turn Assembly: Uniform.Turn.dll Syntax public sealed class TurnServer : IAsyncDisposable Remarks It refuses to relay to DeniedPeers, by default every address that is not public, so it cannot be used to reach the server's own network. Data between two allocations of this server goes from one to the other directly, so clients behind the same router as the server need no NAT hairpinning. Project Kind Status Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Core Spec types shared by clients and servers: IDs, events, API records, canonical JSON Client-Server API types Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Client HTTP client of the Client-Server API Login, sync, rooms, messages, media, devices, keys, backup Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Crypto End-to-end encryption in pure .NET Olm, Megolm, cross-signing, secret storage, backup, key requests, SAS Uniform.Matrix.Hosting Settings and logging for .NET host applications Settings file layers, option catalog, session logs Uniform.Matrix.Gui.Terminal Terminal.Gui components Settings window, log window, dialogs Uniform.Matrix.Client Headless client with local SQLite storage Session, sync, outbox, media cache, encryption, room state Uniform.Chat.Terminal Terminal client app (Terminal.Gui v2) Rooms, messages, files, encryption, settings and logs Uniform.Chat.Avalonia Graphical app shared by desktop and Android (Avalonia) Rooms, messages, files, encryption, verification, notifications on Linux Uniform.Chat.Desktop Graphical app for Windows and Linux Entry point, application menu entry Uniform.Chat.Android Graphical app for Android Entry point; no store release yet Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Server Homeserver protocol: room versions, event format, signing, auth rules Room versions 10, 11 and 12 Uniform.Matrix.Server Homeserver engine on ASP.NET Core and SQLite Accounts, rooms, sync and sliding sync, media, encryption relay, directory, push, calls, federation Uniform.Chat.Server Homeserver app, with or without the dashboard Dashboard, users and rooms admin, settings and logs Building: build the solution and the apps, and make releases. Dependencies point down; the protocol libraries know nothing of storage, hosting or UI: Uniform.Chat.Terminal ──► Uniform.Matrix.Client ──► Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Client ──► Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Core │ │ │ │ │ └──► Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Crypto ──► Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Core │ └───────┐ │ ▼ └──► Uniform.Matrix.Gui.Terminal ──► Uniform.Matrix.Hosting The graphical app uses the same engine, without the terminal components: Uniform.Chat.Desktop ──┐ ├──► Uniform.Chat.Avalonia ──► Uniform.Matrix.Client ──► … Uniform.Chat.Android ──┘ The server side, which also uses Core through Crypto: Uniform.Chat.Server ──► Uniform.Matrix.Server ──► Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Server ──► Uniform.Matrix.Protocol.Crypto │ │ │ └───────────┐ │ ▼ └──► Uniform.Matrix.Gui.Terminal ──► Uniform.Matrix.Hosting The server reuses Core, Crypto (to check key signatures), Hosting and Gui.Terminal, so its settings and log windows are the same as the client's. See Uniform.Matrix.Server for how it works.
